Position Title:

Education Program Coordinator, Program Analyst 1 (Wilsonville)

Job Description:

Education Program Coordinator, Program Analyst 1 (Wilsonville)

Coffee Creek Correctional Facility (CCCF)

Oregon Department of Corrections

The Oregon Department of Corrections (ODOC) is seeking a motivated, collaborative, and forward-thinking individual to join our team as an Education Program Coordinator.

This is an exciting opportunity to make a meaningful difference by building partnerships, expanding access to educational and vocational opportunities, and supporting Adults in Custody (AICs) in achieving their educational goals.

If you are passionate about education, believe in the power of opportunity, and enjoy creating connections that positively impact others, we invite you to be part of our team!

About the Job – Your Role

In this role, you will coordinate educational and vocational programming within a DOC facility, serving as a key connection between community colleges, facility staff, educational volunteers, and agency leadership. You will build partnerships, expand educational opportunities, and help remove barriers to ensure Adults in Custody (AICs) have access to programs that support personal growth, workforce development, and successful reentry.

You will develop and maintain partnerships with community colleges, facility staff, volunteers, and agency leadership to support and expand educational programming. While coordinating communication, programming needs, and daily operations while collaborating with partners to identify new educational and vocational opportunities, pursue grant funding, and recruit educational volunteers.

You will oversee educational program coordination, including scheduling, classroom space, resource allocation, and program expenses. Research best practices, assess program needs, recommend improvements, monitor program effectiveness, and identify opportunities to enhance or expand services. Collaborate with college partners and facility staff to resolve operational challenges and ensure consistent program delivery.

You will assist AICs with accessing educational opportunities by coordinating program applications, eligibility, and enrollment. You will provide guidance on college opportunities and FAFSA applications, respond to questions and concerns, participate in treatment team meetings as appropriate, and coordinate with educational partners and facility staff to address barriers and support AIC participation.

This position is represented by American Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees (AFSCME). This position may be eligible for Police & Fire (P&F) benefits through Public Employees Retirement System (PERS), as defined by statute.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's Degree in Business or Public Administration, Behavioral or Social Sciences, or a degree related to the agency program that demonstrates the capacity for the knowledge and skills; OR

Any combination of experience or education equivalent to three (3) years technical-level experience that typically supports the knowledge and skill requirements listed for the classification

Requested Skills

  • Strong organizational and coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple programs, priorities, and deadlines.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with internal and external partners.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to identify solutions to program and operational challenges.
  • Ability to review information, analyze program needs, and make recommendations for improvements.
  • Commitment to supporting educational access and opportunities for individuals in a correctional setting.
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a dynamic environment while balancing the needs of AICs, educational partners, and facility operations.

Application Information

  • In the Work Experience section of your application make sure to include the dates and duties of all relevant positions and details to support how you meet these attributes. If you do not include education or work experience meeting the minimum qualifications, you will not be considered for the position. Only the candidates whose experience most closely matches the qualifications and requested skills of this position will be invited to interview. Applicants must meet the minimum qualifications on or before the job posting close date.
  • The job posting closes at 11:59 PM (PDT/PST) on the close date. After you submit your application, be sure to respond to the two questionnaires relating to public records requests and veterans’ preference immediately following your submittal. These questions are necessary to complete the application process.
  • Please monitor both your email and Workday account for updates regarding this recruitment.
  • As part of our selection process, we may require additional assessment stages, such as written exercises, to further evaluate candidates’ qualifications. Meaningful participation in these exercises is required for all applicants moving forward in the process. Failure to complete the required exercise(s) within the specified timeframe will result in disqualification from consideration. All candidates who successfully complete these screening stages and meet the necessary requirements will advance to the next stage in the selection process.
  • Please save a copy of this job announcement for reference, as it is not available for you to view after the announcement deadline.

Working Conditions

Regular attendance is an essential function required to meet the demands of this job and to provide necessary services.

Work will be performed in an adult correctional facility and will have interaction with AICs. Possible encounters with abusive/hostile AICs pose a risk of personal injury and/or being taken hostage and death. Exposure to materials of graphic nature, and to dangerous situations does exist.

Work includes extended sitting time at a computer terminal, involvement in telephone conversations, writing various documents, data entry, bending, lifting, stooping, and stretching.

Your working schedule will be Monday through Friday 7:30 – 4pm

About the Department

The Oregon Department of Corrections is responsible for over 12,000 adults in custody in 12 state prisons throughout Oregon. It advises and evaluates counties regarding administration of probation and parole programs supervising more than 24,000 offenders in Oregon communities. The mission is to protect communities, promote accountability, and transform lives.

The Oregon Department of Corrections serves a diverse and changing population of people who are incarcerated and on supervision. We commit to creating an organization both reflecting the diversity of the population we serve and ensuring all employees thrive in a culture of safety, trust, and belonging. We strive to be an anti-racist corrections system. Welcoming, inclusive, and respectful of all people. Free of discrimination, harassment, and retaliation.

The Department offers a variety of programs and opportunity to create a safe and healthy environment to for our staff, volunteers, and adults in custody. Joining the Oregon Department of Corrections is joining a team working for the benefit of our communities through innovative and proven correctional practices.

Benefits

The salary range listed above is for non-PERS qualifying applicants. PERS qualifying applicants may be eligible for an adjusted range to reflect an additional 6.95%.

The State of Oregon provides a generous benefit package, which includes:

  • Family health, vision, and dental insurance

description:
Vuoi lavorare in un’azienda che ti dà la possibilità di trasformare positivamente il mondo in cui viviamo?

In Bureau Veritas crediamo che lasciare il segno sia una sfida e un’opportunità per ognuno di noi, un’occasione per generare un impatto, un legame con il futuro, una testimonianza di crescita e sviluppo.

Far parte della nostra organizzazione non vuol dire semplicemente lavorare ma anche contribuire alla costruzione di un mondo fondato sulla fiducia.

Dal 1828, Bureau Veritas è leader a livello mondiale nei servizi di ispezione, verifica di conformità e certificazione. Digital Transformation, Energy Transition, Cybersecurity, Sostenibilità, Construction, Export e Logistica, Food, Healthcare, sono solo alcuni dei servizi e degli ambiti all’interno dei quali il Gruppo opera.

La risorsa sarà inserita all’interno del team TLS (Transports and Logistics Services).


In particolare, la risorsa si occuperà delle seguenti attività:

  • Verifica deli imballaggi per merci pericolose;

title: Technical Editor
description:

title: Information Technology Plans and Resource Manager
description:
Torch Technologies

Thank you for your interest in employment with Torch Technologies. We are a 100% employee-owned, Certified Great Place To Work and named Best Places to Work in Huntsville/Madison County, headquartered in Huntsville, AL. Our team provides superior research, development, and engineering services to the Federal Government and Department of War. As one of the nation’s top 100 defense companies, the services we provide directly support the men and women who serve our country. Our corporate mission sums up the pride our employee-owners take in the work we do: “Lighting the Pathway of Freedom”. And, as a Certified Evergreen ESOP, we have made the commitment to grow and sustain our company for the next 100 years! Come grow with us!

Torch Technologies is seeking a highly motivated Information Technology (IT) Plans and Resources Manager to serve as the senior task leader and program manager supporting the Air Force Research Laboratory, Detachment 6 (AFRL/Det 6) at the Eglin Research Site (ERS).

The successful candidate will lead the design, development, integration, and sustainment of secure, scalable, mission-aligned solutions which improve workforce efficiency, data quality, business-process execution, and operational readiness. This role requires close collaboration with government stakeholders, supporting operational planning, assessment, cybersecurity, and technical team leadership within complex United States Air Force (USAF), Department of War (DoW), or comparable enterprise environments.

The successful candidate will also serve as Torch Technologies, Inc. Group Leader and Supervisor for the team of Torch employee-owners supporting the Government customer in these efforts at Eglin AFB, FL.


As a Information Technology (IT) Plans and Resources Manager your duties will include the following, but are not limited to:

  • Provide day-to-day operational management of Service/Agency capability development projects.
  • Collaborate closely with Technical Managers, Stakeholders, and Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) across multiple directorates
  • Support operational planning, capability development, event integration, analysis, and reporting activities.
  • Developing, managing, and executing IT budgets; forecasting expenditures; allocating resources; and identifying funding gaps.
  • Managing multiple IT initiatives, tracking milestones, managing dependencies, and reporting program performance to senior leadership.
  • Develop and support program documentation, including Implementation Directives, Management Plans, and monthly reporting.
  • Support and develop various briefings/schedules of program status and procurement tasks to senior management.

Technical Leadership, Collaboration and Documentation

  • Provide strategic technical direction, mentorship, structured development, and quality oversight to developers, automation specialists, network engineers, cybersecurity personnel, and other technical team members.
  • Establish IT governance processes, develop policies, manage configuration and change control boards, and prioritize IT investments.
  • Translate mission needs into actionable IT requirements, develop justifications, and prioritize competing requirements.
  • Build effective working relationships among mission stakeholders, system owners, developers, cybersecurity teams, infrastructure teams, and enterprise IT organizations.
  • Communicate technical concepts, implementation options, risks, timelines, dependencies, and recommendations to both technical and executive-level audiences.

  • U.S. Citizenship.
  • Bachelor’s degree and 5+ years of military or relevant operational experience.
  • Demonstrated expertise in business processes and IT operations management.
  • Program management experience including cost, schedule, and performance oversight.
  • Experience evaluating operational requirements and emergent requirements.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including briefing senior leadership.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.
  • Active TS/SCI security clearance required (must be able to maintain)

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree or relevant certifications in program management, operations, or related field.
  • 10+ years of Leadership experience within a DoW organization, military service, or federal agency.
  • Professional certifications relevant to IT management, cybersecurity, program management, or agile delivery such as CISSP, CISM, or PMP certifications or equivalent.
  • Experience supporting USAF, Department of War, federal, defense, research and development, or similar mission-critical environments.
  • Experience working with cross-functional teams and government stakeholders.
  • Strong technical writing, reporting, and briefing experience.
  • Understand Risk Management Framework (RMF), National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) standards, cybersecurity controls, authorization requirements, and cybersecurity implications of IT investments.
  • Experience supporting enterprise-level IT operations.

title: Senior Product Manager
location: New York, New York, United States; Princeton, New Jersey, United States
description:
Noom is on a mission to help people live better, longer. We’re a consumer-led digital health company, connecting people to content, coaching, community, and clinicians to build lasting habits and live healthier lives. We’re a high-growth organization powered by science, technology, and world-class talent. When you join Noom, on any team, you’ll see the impact of your work on the world.

Our Product Team

Noom’s Product team builds experiences that help people turn health insights into lasting habits. We bring together behavioral science, technology, and a deep understanding of our members to make healthier living more personalized, engaging, and accessible.

Our team connects health data, platform capabilities, and intuitive app experiences to help members better understand their health and take meaningful action.

About the Role

We’re seeking a Senior Product Manager to shape how personal health data becomes useful, engaging experiences across Noom. Reporting to a VP of Product, you’ll lead a cross-functional team responsible for both the underlying capabilities and the member-facing experiences that make this possible.

You’ll take ownership of an emerging product area, building on its initial foundations to develop new app experiences, personalized insights, and activities that support healthier habits. This role requires a well-rounded product leader who can think through backend systems and data flows while partnering closely with Design to create thoughtful, intuitive experiences.

Working alongside other product teams, you’ll help connect capabilities across Noom so members benefit from a more cohesive, personalized experience.

You Will

  • Own your team’s product strategy, roadmap, and execution, balancing foundational platform investments with member-facing improvements
  • Turn personal health data into clear, actionable app experiences that help members understand their progress and build healthier habits
  • Partner closely with Design to develop new screens, surfaces, and activities that make complex information useful and engaging
  • Work with Engineering to define scalable capabilities for data access, personalized insights, and timely, contextually relevant engagement
  • Collaborate with teams building AI coaching and other personalized experiences to make health data useful across the broader Noom app
  • Align priorities, dependencies, and ownership with adjacent product teams working toward a shared member experience
  • Translate member research, product data, and business priorities into clear requirements and focused development plans
  • Define success metrics and use experimentation, member feedback, and analysis to improve adoption, engagement, and retention
  • Apply thoughtful judgment to privacy, transparency, and member trust when developing experiences involving personal health data

About You

You’re equally comfortable discussing how data moves through a system and working with a designer to make that data meaningful to a member. You can connect technical investments to a compelling product experience, make clear tradeoffs, and keep a team focused as an emerging product area evolves.

You bring strong consumer instincts, curiosity about health technology, and a collaborative approach. You’re excited to build on an early product foundation and help shape what comes next.

You Have

  • 6+ years of product management experience, with a track record of delivering consumer-facing products and measurable results
  • Experience building wearable products, strongly preferred, or other health-focused hardware products with companion digital experiences
  • An understanding of the distinct user expectations, privacy considerations, and trust required when connecting health devices and software
  • Strong UX judgment and experience partnering closely with designers to build intuitive mobile experiences
  • Comfort taking ownership in an evolving product area and adapting plans as you learn
  • Experience with AI-generated insights, personalized recommendations, or AI coaching; at minimum, the ability to reason through the systems needed to support these experiences
  • Strong systems thinking, with the ability to reason through data pipelines, integrations, backend services, and dependencies alongside engineering partners
  • Experience balancing platform development with user-facing product work and explaining how each contributes to member and business outcomes
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, including experience aligning multiple teams around shared priorities
  • Strong analytical skills and experience using research, experimentation, and product metrics to guide decisions
  • A passion for helping people improve their health through thoughtful, accessible technology

What Makes This Job Amazing

  • Shape an emerging product area. Build on an early foundation with substantial room to influence the roadmap and member experience.
  • Connect technology to everyday behavior. Help members turn personal health information into practical actions and lasting habits.
  • Own work across the product stack. Combine platform thinking, experience design, and personalization in one role.
  • Build with strong partners. Work closely with experienced design, engineering, and product teammates.
  • Make a meaningful impact. Create experiences that strengthen the programs members already rely on to improve their health.

What You’ll Earn and Enjoy

  • Pay that reflects your impact. Compensation benchmarked to the market and shaped by your impact and value.
  • Investment in your future. A 401(k) with company match to help you build long-term financial security.
  • Time to truly recharge. Paid holidays, flexible and generous PTO, Summer Fridays, and a company-wide Summer Break week so the whole team can unplug together.
  • Care that covers it all. Access to top-tier medical plans for you and your family, including a premium-free plan option, alongside dental, vision, and life insurance.
  • Support for growing families. Paid parental leave to give you the time and flexibility to focus on what matters most.
  • And more to help you thrive. Stock awards, a performance-based bonus, and exclusive access to Noom’s products, so you can grow with us, win with us, and enjoy what we build.

The base salary range for this position is $164,000-$215,000. Actual compensation is determined by job-related factors, including experience, skills, qualifications, and location.

This role is eligible for our NYC or Princeton office locations, operating on a hybrid schedule (2 days per week on-site).

More About Noom

Noom is a leading whole-person health platform on a mission to help people live better, longer. We combine personalized medication with the science of behavior change and psychology, to help people build lasting habits and live longer, healthier lives. With nationally-recognized, holistic programs spanning weight, diabetes prevention, GLP-1 support, menopause, longevity, and more, we serve millions through health plans, employers, and direct-to-consumer offerings. As a trailblazer in the world of health and wellness, Noom makes healthy living easy, fun, and deeply rewarding.

We're more than a health tech company—we're a movement. This belief extends to our culture: we empower our people to think big, act boldly, and take pride in their contributions to shaping the future of health. We've been named one of the Best Places to Work by Inc., Fortune, Glassdoor, and Quartz—including honors for technology and diversity.

Join us in shaping the future of health. You'll be part of a passionate, mission-driven team working to make the world a healthier place—one habit at a time.

To help protect against potential hiring scams, please be aware that all email communications from the Noom Talent team and/or hiring managers will come only from an @noom.com email address. Please ignore any messaging or communication from other domains (e.g. @noom.team). Noom will never ask you for personal payment, require you to purchase equipment, conduct an interview process or messaging exchange via Microsoft Teams, or extend a job offer without the completion of a multi-step interview process featuring a combination of phone, Zoom, and in-person interviews, as well as references. title: Unit Manager - Production Services
description:
Requisition ID: 40419


Unit Manager – Production Services

Cheers to Creating an Incredible Tomorrow!

At Molson Coors, we tackle big challenges and defy the status quo. With a proud legacy of excellence, an incredible portfolio of beer, seltzers, spirits, and non-alcohol brands, and a bold vision for our future, we're on the path to transforming the beverage industry. That requires remarkable individuals who are curious, tenacious, and never afraid to fail forward.

We seek, value, and respect everyone's unique perspectives and experiences, knowing that we are stronger together. We collaborate as a team and celebrate each other's successes.

Here's to crafting careers and creating new legacies.

Crafted Highlights

In the role of Unit Manager – Production Services, working in our Fort Worth Brewery, you will lead production planning, scheduling, inventory management, and distribution operations to ensure efficient product flow from brewing through customer delivery. You will be responsible for optimizing brewery throughput, balancing customer demand with operational capacity, and driving supply chain performance through effective planning, execution, and continuous improvement.

Working closely with brewery leadership, corporate supply planning, customer service, logistics providers, and other cross-functional partners, you will align brewing, packaging, warehousing, and shipping activities to maximize service, inventory performance, and operational efficiency. Leveraging data and performance insights, you will identify opportunities, mitigate risks, resolve constraints, and support effective decision-making across the brewery.

You will also lead and develop a team of planning and scheduling professionals while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and operational excellence. Compliance with all safety, food safety, quality, and regulatory requirements is essential to ensuring product quality, operational performance, and customer satisfaction.

What You'll Be Brewing

  • Lead the development and optimization of production, shipping, and distribution schedules to ensure efficient product flow, maximize service levels, and support customer demand while minimizing operational costs and complexity.
  • Develop, execute, and continuously improve brewery throughput plans by aligning brewing, packaging, warehousing, and shipping activities to maximize asset utilization and operational efficiency.
  • Partner with production leadership to balance capacity, inventory targets, service requirements, and operational priorities, making schedule adjustments as needed to address changing business demands.
  • Oversee finished goods inventory management to ensure product availability, maintain inventory accuracy, minimize waste, and support customer fulfillment objectives.
  • Monitor and analyze production and inventory performance, identifying risks, constraints, and opportunities to improve operational effectiveness and supply chain performance.
  • Serve as the primary liaison between brewery operations, corporate supply planning, customer service, logistics providers, and other key stakeholders to ensure alignment on production schedules, inventory availability, and fulfillment priorities.
  • Communicate production plan changes, operational risks, and supply constraints while facilitating cross-functional collaboration and data-driven decision-making.
  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of production planning and scheduling professionals, fostering a culture of accountability, engagement, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
  • Drive talent development, performance management, succession planning, and organizational effectiveness initiatives to build a high-performing team.
  • Ensure compliance with all company policies, safety standards, quality systems, and food safety requirements while supporting organizational change and continuous improvement efforts.

Key Ingredients:

  • 5-8 years of progressive experience in supply chain, production scheduling, manufacturing operations, logistics, or related operational leadership roles.
  • Experience leading and developing teams within a manufacturing, brewery, or production environment.
  • Strong knowledge of end-to-end manufacturing, supply chain, inventory management, distribution operations, capacity planning, and production scheduling.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage cross-functional supply chain processes while influencing stakeholders across multiple organizational levels.
  • Proven leadership, coaching, and talent development capabilities with a track record of building high-performing teams.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Working knowledge of financial principles, operational budgeting, cost management, and resource optimization.
  • Knowledge of food safety and quality systems, including GMP, HACCP, and SQF standards.
  • Proficiency with ERP systems, production planning tools, inventory management systems, reporting applications, and data-driven decision-making methodologies.
  • You have a Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Engineering, Manufacturing, Logistics, or a related technical field OR OR equivalent experience (4+ years) in the field of production planning
  • Experience within the beverage, food, consumer packaged goods (CPG), or other high-volume manufacturing environments.
  • Experience applying continuous improvement methodologies such as Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or World Class Supply Chain principles.
  • Demonstrated success leading supply chain or operational improvement initiatives that enhance service levels, inventory performance, throughput, and overall operational efficiency.

Other Key Ingredients:

  • You thrive in a fast-paced, complex manufacturing environment.
  • You love a challenge. You complete complex projects quickly and adeptly with your understanding of the business priorities
  • You build relationships and collaborate to get to the desired outcome
  • You take accountability for results – acting with integrity and honoring commitments
  • You have a thirst for learning – you are always looking for ways to learn and help one another grow You exhibit our core values

Beverage Bonuses:

  • Participation in our Total Rewards program with a competitive base salary, incentive plans, parental leave, health, dental, vision, retirement plan options with incredible employer match, generous paid time off plans, an engaging Wellness Program, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) with amazing resources
  • On site Pub, access to cool brand clothing and swag, top events and, of course... free beer and beverages!
  • We care about our People and Planet and have challenged ourselves with stretch goals around our key priorities
  • We care about our communities, and play our part to make a difference – from charitable donations to hitting the streets together to build parks, giving back to the community is part of our culture and who we are
  • Engagement with a variety of Business Resource Groups, which can provide volunteer opportunities, leadership experience, and networking through the organization
  • Ability to grow and develop your career centered around our First Choice Learning opportunities
  • Work within a fast paced and innovative company, meeting passionate colleagues and partners with diverse backgrounds and experiences


Job Posting Grade: 12

Molson Coors is an equal opportunity employer. We invite applications from candidates of all backgrounds, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status or any other characteristic. If you have a disability and believe you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or recruitment processes, please e-mail jobs@molsoncoors.com.


Pay and Benefits:

At Molson Coors, we’re committed to paying people fairly and equitably for the work they do.


Job Posting Total Rewards Offerings: $97,400.00 - $127,900.00 (posting salary range) + 15% target short term incentive + $23,000 on average spent on benefits per employee, including but not limited to health, dental, vision, retirement with above market employer match, wellness incentives and EAP + paid time off (including holidays, vacation days and sick days).


The posting range provided above for salary is what we, in good faith, believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We ultimately pay based on a number of non-discriminatory factors that inform pay decisions including but not limited to the required work location, previous work experience, skill set and internal equity.

title: Director of Institutional Effectiveness (Department Director II)
description:
Join our Team at Portland Community College

Please Note: PCC currently limits employment to individuals residing in Oregon and Washington. Employment offers are contingent upon the ability to establish residence in Oregon or Washington.

Portland Community College will also ensure that applicants requiring reasonable accommodation for the hiring process are provided for. If reasonable accommodation is needed, please contact the PCC Talent Acquisition Team at pccjobs@pcc.edu.

Portland Community College is the largest post-secondary institution in Oregon and 19th largest in the nation, serving approximately 80,000 full- and part-time students. With four comprehensive campuses, five workforce training and education centers, and 200 community locations in the Portland metropolitan area, our unique role is to make high-quality education accessible to everyone, creating opportunities for our students and contributing to the economic development of our community.

What You'll Do and Who We Are Looking For

Under the direction of the Dean of Institutional Effectiveness and Planning, oversees the Office of Institutional Effectiveness. Incumbents have overall accountability for providing leadership in long-range planning, program development, problem solving, and staff development in an assigned administrative department. Responds to inquiries from College departments, the community, and/or external agencies and supervises administrative services professionals, paraprofessionals, and technical/support staff. May serve as a member of the President’s Leadership Team.


Distinguishing Characteristics

The Department Director II is the second level in a three level Department Director series. The Department Director II is distinguished from other Department Directors by its responsibility for a department moderate in scope and complexity. Areas of responsibility require significant job knowledge base. The impact of work and decisions can affect the entire District and will have a longer impact than Level I positions.


Full Classification Description listing Typical Duties, and Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities for this position:


Minimum Qualifications:

Master’s degree in education, behavioral or social science, public policy, or related field with emphasis on research, planning and assessment activities related to higher education (relevant experience may substitute for the degree requirement on a year-for-year basis).


Five years of experience in research, planning and assessment activities related to higher education. Management and supervisory experience is desired.


Success Criteria: (throughout the screening process, you will be evaluated based on your demonstration of the following criteria):


- Data Literacy & Capacity Building: Demonstrated skill in designing and delivering data literacy initiatives and tools that empower non-technical academic and administrative leaders.

- Cross-Functional & Cross-Pathway Collaboration: Experience co-chairing college-wide governance committees, fostering cross-pathway collaboration, and building strong working relationships with Academic Affairs, Student Affairs, Human Resources, Finance, Operations, and executive leadership.

- Web Communication & Data Dissemination: Experience leading the redesign and management of public and internal web pages to make institutional information accessible and transparent to the broader college community.

- Technical & Statistical Proficiency: Familiarity and experience with SQL, statistical packages (R, Python, SPSS, or SAS), and modern dashboarding platforms (Tableau, Power BI, etc.), and use of generative AI-LLMs in research and decision-support.

- Futures Studies, Change Management & Operational Agility: Experience with strategic forecasting (including environmental scanning) and exceptional change management capabilities to support organizational growth, process improvements, and the integration of evolving division initiatives.



Preferred Qualifications:

- Education & Experience: Master's degree in Higher Education Administration, Institutional Research, Applied Statistics/Data Analytics, Public Policy, or a related quantitative or analytical field preferred (or equivalent extensive professional experience in institutional research, data analytics, or higher education leadership); Ph.D. or Ed.D. welcomed. A Bachelor's degree and a high level of relevant experience may substitute for a Master's degree.

- Leadership Experience: 4+ years of administrative and analytical leadership in institutional effectiveness, research, or strategic planning – preferably within a community college or university setting, supporting alignment with executive leadership and Dean portfolio objectives.

- Team Leadership: Proven track record of managing, coordinating, and/or mentoring multi-disciplinary teams across data analytics, programmer/analysts, labor market research, and/or strategic planning.

Preferred Advanced Knowledge

- Futures Studies & Strategic Planning: Familiarity with strategic forecasting, environmental scanning, and embedding "Futures Thinking" frameworks into organizational planning.

- Data Governance & Enterprise Architecture: In-depth knowledge of higher education enterprise data architecture, data stewardship principles, data quality management, and co-leading data governance frameworks in partnership with Information Technology leadership.

- Modern Data Warehousing & Self-Service BI: Expertise in data warehouse design concepts, ETL processes, and user-centered self-service business intelligence (BI) solutions that facilitate data-informed decision-making.

Institutional Metrics & Program Review Analytics: Deep understanding of developing, implementing, and communicating institutional success metrics, key performance indicators (KPIs), continuous improvement analytics, and aligning academic program review with college-wide strategic plans and budget cycles.

Survey Methodology & Research Infrastructure: Advanced knowledge of survey design, sampling methodologies, survey administration policies, and routine data collection frameworks.

- State/Federal Reporting & Accreditation Standards: Comprehensive knowledge of state and federal reporting requirements (e.g., IPEDS, financial aid compliance) and regional accreditation data integration (e.g., NWCCU standards).

Why You'll Love Working Here

The PCC district encompasses a 1,500-square-mile area in northwest Oregon and offers two-year degrees, one-year certificate programs, short-term training, alternative education, pre-college courses and life-long learning. As part of our College community, you’ll enjoy:

  • A collaborative and inspiring campus community

  • Opportunities for learning and professional development

Portland Community College embraces equity and inclusion as a priority. We are committed to building a community with a variety of backgrounds, skills, views, and life experiences. The more we value equity and inclusion, the more we will add value to the work we do and how we serve our students, engage with each other, and the Oregon Community that we serve. Creating a culture that honors equity and inclusion is our objective and the smart path forward.

Position Grade

Management N

Employment Type

Full time

Total Rewards Package / What We Offer

  • Comprehensive benefit package designed to provide employees and their families, including domestic partners, with access to a broad range of benefit options. Includes Health, Dental, and Vision options, Group Life, Long-term Disability, Long-term Care, and Auto and Home Insurance programs

  • Oregon PERS contribution - PCC currently fully funds the Oregon Public Employees Retirement System (PERS/OPSRP) pension and contributes an additional 6% into the employee's Individual Account Program under PERS/OPSRP

  • Tax deferred annuity program and a deferred compensation program where employees may save additional pre-tax dollars for retirement

  • PCC provides a tuition waiver for you, your spouse/domestic partner, and dependent children under 24 years of age, as well as partial tuition reimbursement for full-time employees at other accredited institutions

  • Free access to the sport centers / campus gymnasiums, performing arts, and cultural events

  • Generous Paid Leave (Pro-rated by FTE for Part-Time Employees) reference Management and Confidential Employee Handbook

    • 14.67 hours of vacation leave per month

    • 1 day of sick leave per month

    • 12 paid holidays

    • PCC Winter Break (when College is Closed)

    • 24 hours of personal leave per year

More detailed information on the benefits plans, who is eligible, and how to enroll or make changes can be found at . Please email PCCBenefits@pcc.edu if you have any questions.

How We Determine Initial Salary Placement

Minimum $113,994 to range midpoint of $139,642. Placement will generally not exceed the mid-point, based on qualifications, experience, and internal equity.

Oregon Veterans' Preference in Public Employment

Portland Community College complies with the Oregon Veterans' Preference in Public Employment law which provides qualifying veterans and disabled veterans with preference in employment. You will be given instructions during the application process to claim Veterans' Preference in the recruitment of this position, and to provide the documents required for verification of eligibility. Please do not send your documentation to the hiring manager directly. For verification of eligibility, please submit the following documentation:

  • Veterans: DD214

  • Disabled Veterans: DD214 and Letter from the Department of VA

Notice of the Availability of the Annual Security Report

Pursuant to the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy and Campus Crime Statistics Act (Clery Act), you may view Portland Community College’s (PCC) most recent Annual Security Report (ASR) on the Department of Public Safety website. The ASR contains current security and safety-related policy disclosure statements, emergency preparedness and evacuation information, crime prevention and sexual assault prevention information and resources, and drug and alcohol prevention programming. The ASR also contains crime statistics for Clery Act crimes which occurred on PCC properties for the last three calendar years. Paper copies of the ASR are available upon request at all Department of Public Safety offices.

PCC Employment Offers are Contingent Upon the Successful Completion of a Criminal Background Check

Please note that Portland Community College is not currently able to provide visa (e.g. H1-B Visa) sponsorship for potential employees.

Contact PCC at pccjobs@pcc.edu if you have questions

title: Tax Analyst
description:
Yext (NYSE: YEXT) is the enterprise agentic marketing platform. Built on the world's most comprehensive structured data platform for local businesses, Yext gives brands and their partners the visibility intelligence to win every moment of discovery – across AI and traditional search. Yext's API-first architecture connects structured data to APIs, MCP servers, and generative interfaces, so partners and developers can build purpose-built experiences on the same infrastructure powering Yext's own products. Thousands of brands and digital marketing partners in financial services, healthcare, retail, hospitality, and food rely on Yext to manage, measure, and optimize visibility at scale. For more information, visit .

Yext is expanding its International Operation Center and is looking for a talented and dynamic Tax Analyst to be part of the tax function based in India. The Tax Analyst will report to the Senior Tax Analyst in Hyderabad and work very closely with the tax team located in the US. The candidate is critical in defining and managing the processes for local tax filings and requirements, and will assist the US team on direct and indirect tax related tasks. The Tax Analyst will need to interact directly with other finance members across the organization as well as with external tax advisors. The ideal candidate is someone who’s self-motivated, a quick learner with excellent organizational and communication skills, and demonstrates strong initiative, ownership and passion.

What You’ll Do

  • Work with external service providers and internal tax team members to accurately and timely file all local Indian direct and indirect tax returns; maintain and monitor local tax filing calendar
  • Prepare, collate, and review global indirect tax returns(VAT/GST) across EMEA, APAC, and Canada regions in coordination with external advisors,ensuring compliance with local filing deadlines.
  • Assist in monthly tax account reconciliations, calculations, journal entries and tax return preparations
  • Develop knowledge of both Direct and Indirect Tax laws and apply to the business and keep up-to-date with changes
  • Develop in-depth knowledge of tools and applications supporting Tax processes
  • Assist the US tax team with inputs / preparations of the quarterly and annual US GAAP ASC740 Income Tax Provision calculations for the Yext India entity
  • At times assist with tax audits including gathering information, and assembling responses to auditor inquiries
  • Proactively identify areas for process improvements and implement solutions to automate existing workpapers and streamline processes
  • Assist in SOX process implementation for Yext India entity

What You Have

  • Minimum 2-4 years of relevant working experience in handling local Indian direct/indirect tax calculations, filings, and requirements
  • Solid understanding of accounting in the general ledger and financial statements, US GAAP accounting knowledge a plus
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Excellent computer skills and advanced Excel skills (Pivots, SUMIFS, INDEXMATCH, etc.)
  • Self-starter who is able to be self-reliant and motivated to take on tasks and demonstrate the ability to work with service providers to drive tasks and projects to completion
  • Sense of responsibility, initiative and high-quality work standards
  • Strong willingness to work flexible hours with global business from time to time
  • Must be able to multitask, work efficiently under tight deadlines and proactively track and report progress
  • Self-motivated to apply learned experiences and leverage best practices

Bonus Points

  • Prior experience / knowledge with US Sales Tax/European VAT or other global indirect taxes a plus, keen interest in international taxes including emerging taxes, e.g., Digital Services Taxes
  • Experience with Netsuite ERP system/Zuora billing system/Avalara sales tax software a plus
  • Chartered Accountant / MBA with Bachelor’s degree in Accounting
  • Prior working experience at Big 4 Public Accounting Firms or in house tax function of a US multinational companies

Perks and Benefits

At Yext, we take pride in our diverse workforce and prioritize creating an engaged and connected working environment. Our ambitious mission is to transform the enterprise with AI search, and we know that to achieve that, we need a global team of innovators, visionary thought leaders, and enthusiastic collaborators passionate about making a meaningful impact in the world and contributing to an extraordinary culture.

We believe that people do their best when they feel their best — and to feel their best, they must be well-informed, fuelled, and rested. To ensure our employees are at their best, we offer a wide range of benefits and perks, including:

  • Performance-Based Compensation: We offer an attractive bonus structure and stock options for eligible positions.
  • Comprehensive Leave Package: Our leave package includes Paid Time Off (PTO), Parental Leave, Sick Leave, Casual Leave, Bereavement Leave, National Holidays, and Floating Holidays to ensure a healthy work-life balance.
  • Health & Wellness Offerings: We provide medical insurance with 7L coverage, including enhanced parental and outpatient department (OPD) coverage for you, your spouse, two dependent children, and two parents (as applicable and subject to eligibility requirements).
  • Relocation Benefits: We offer relocation assistance and an allowance to eligible candidates to help ease your transition.
  • World-Class Office & Building Amenities: Our office has a top-notch infrastructure, including gaming rooms, a plush pantry, and breakout areas.

#LI-RD1
#LI-Onsite

Yext is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a results-driven, engaging culture where every employee has the opportunity to contribute to the success of the Company, perform at the highest possible level, and grow their skills and capabilities. title: Physics AI Scientist III
description:
Who We Are


Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology.


What We Offer


Salary:

$161,000.00 - $221,000.00

Location:

Santa Clara,CA

You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more.

At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits.

Role Summary

Develop next-generation AI models for semiconductor engineering by combining scientific domain knowledge with modern machine learning. Build physics-aware surrogate models, foundation models, and optimization workflows that accelerate simulation and engineering design.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop Scientific AI models that bridge scientific computing, physics-based simulation and machine learning for physics and chemistry-based engineering problems.
  • Design and train surrogate models, operator-learning models, and foundation models for scientific simulations.
  • Collaborate with domain experts to formulate AI solutions for complex engineering challenges.
  • Develop scalable data generation, training, validation and deployment workflows for Scientific AI models.
  • Publish technical innovations and drive adoption of Scientific AI across engineering applications.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • Experience applying machine learning to real-world scientific or engineering problems.
  • Strong background in scientific machine learning and numerical simulation.

title: Sr. Principal Autonomous Networks & Agentic AI Architect – 5G Mobile Core
location: USA:WA:Bothell / 20309 North Creek Pkwy - Adm (bothell 7):20309 N Creek Pkwy @ Bldg L
description:
This is a full-time onsite role based in the location(s) posted and is performed from the designated work location five days per week. No relocation is offered.


At AT&T, we're building the next generation of autonomous network operations. We're looking for a senior technical leader who can bring together 5G Mobile Core, network automation, AIOps, intent-driven networking, and agentic AI to move network operations toward true closed-loop autonomy.


As a Sr. Principal Member of Technical Staff, you'll set technical direction and lead the architecture, engineering, and delivery of autonomous capabilities across AT&T's Mobile Core. You'll help advance Mobile Core use cases across the TM Forum Autonomous Network maturity model, designing systems capable of understanding intent, evaluating network conditions, making governed decisions, taking action, and continuously learning from outcomes.


This is a highly technical leadership role for someone who can move comfortably between architecture, software engineering, AI/ML, telecom standards, network operations, and large-scale execution.


What You'll Do:

  • Lead the architecture and engineering of Autonomous Network capabilities for AT&T's Mobile Core, advancing use cases across TM Forum AN Levels 1–5.
  • Define intent-driven architectures that translate business and operational intent into policies, decisions, and automated network actions.
  • Establish the reference architecture for agentic network operations, including how AI agents interact with network functions, OSS platforms, observability systems, APIs, and automation tools.
  • Design and deploy closed-loop, self-healing systems capable of detecting network conditions, determining corrective actions, executing changes, and validating outcomes.
  • Architect real-time telemetry, topology, event, and network-data pipelines that provide autonomous systems with accurate network state.
  • Apply network analytics and digital twins to predict issues, simulate network behavior, and validate automated actions before production deployment.
  • Develop and operationalize LLM/AI agents, including model selection, tuning, evaluation, tool integration, orchestration, and lifecycle management.
  • Build AI-assisted testing and automation frameworks that accelerate certification, improve defect detection, and increase deployment confidence.
  • Establish responsible automation controls through policy-as-code, human-in-the-loop approvals, blast-radius limits, automated rollback, explainability, and auditability.
  • Design security controls for agentic environments, including agent identity, least-privilege access, token-based authentication, secrets management, credential lifecycle management, and protections against prompt injection and tool misuse.
  • Perform deep technical troubleshooting and root cause analysis using logs, network KPIs, telemetry, and packet-level diagnostics.
  • Define and measure autonomy outcomes including touchless operations, MTTD/MTTR, false-positive rates, and automated-change success.
  • Influence supplier roadmaps so network functions provide automation-ready APIs, telemetry, and control points.
  • Represent AT&T in industry standards organizations including TM Forum, 3GPP SA5, and ETSI ZSM, translating emerging standards into implementable network architectures.
  • Mentor engineers and establish technical direction across teams adopting AI-driven and autonomous network operations.

What You'll Bring:

  • Deep expertise in telecommunications network architecture and automation, ideally within large-scale Mobile Core environments.
  • Strong understanding of 5G Standalone Core architecture, network functions, protocols, lifecycle management, configuration management, and operational workflows.
  • Demonstrated expertise in TM Forum Autonomous Networks and intent-driven network management.
  • Hands-on experience designing agentic AI and closed-loop automation systems, including LLM-based agents, tool integration, guardrails, evaluation, and governance.
  • Strong background in AIOps, ML-enabled automation, observability, network analytics, and production AI/ML architectures.
  • Ability to bridge traditional network engineering with modern cloud-native software engineering, AI/ML, GitOps, APIs, telemetry, and automation.
  • Experience architecting highly available, scalable distributed systems with a focus on reliability, performance, security, and operational efficiency.
  • Proven ability to establish technical direction and drive complex, cross-functional engineering initiatives from architecture through production.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to influence engineering, operations, suppliers, standards organizations, and senior leadership.
  • A hands-on, execution-oriented mindset with the ability to turn emerging AI and autonomous-network concepts into production-grade solutions.

What You'll Need:

  • Extensive experience in network automation, system architecture, AI/ML engineering, or telecom software engineering.
  • Advanced knowledge of 5G SA Mobile Core technologies, protocols, and procedures, including HTTP/2 and mTLS.
  • Hands-on development experience with Python and/or Go.

The Director of Information Security is responsible for developing, implementing and monitoring a strategic, comprehensive enterprise cyber security and IT risk management program. The Director of Information Security provides the vision and leadership necessary to manage the risk to the organization and will ensure business alignment, effective governance, system and product availability, integrity and confidentiality. The Director of Information Security is an integral part of the Information Security team supporting our customers.


Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Conduct a thorough assessment of the company’s security needs, priorities and opportunities in order to visualize, create, and execute on an information security program
  • Design and develop an information security roadmap to align and scale with company growth
  • Lead security assessment and testing processes, including but not limited to penetration testing, vulnerability management, and secure software development at a global level
  • Plan for and manage incident response plans while minimizing effect on the business
  • Develop and extend security tooling and automation efforts across the organization
  • Proactively identify security issues and potential threats and continuously build processes and design systems to watch for and protect against them
  • Lead compliance activities including external audits, regulatory compliance projects, and overall information security reviews
  • Educate the organization about these threats and implement threat protection measures
  • Serve as cross-functional leader and provide direction to key, accountable stakeholders in a matrix environment with dotted-line reports imbedded within the business
  • Serve as the information security expert in front of the Executive team
  • Advocate for secure application and infrastructure best practices, ensuring a security presence at all stages of the software development lifecycle
  • Manage relationships with external information security technology vendors and specialized information security professional services firms
  • Attract, develop, and retain a highly talented team as the information security program grows

Skills:

  • Experience developing, maintaining, and implementing an Information Security Program (ISP) including policy and strategy development, preferably in higher education.
  • Experience addressing information security-related issues involving identity and access management, intrusion detection, forensics, incident management, risk management and/or auditing.
  • Experience evaluating and providing guidance on information security software and hardware acquisitions, IT services, cloud-based solutions, and mobility
  • Knowledge of security assessment and testing tools.
  • Experience with developing and managing an information security awareness and training program.
  • Experience with information security and compliance-related issues (e.g. FERPA, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, GLBA, copyright and software piracy).
  • Experience in managing and negotiating vendor contracts and agreements.
  • Ability to communicate effectively in writing and oral presentations.
  • Strong business acumen and a collaborative, influential partner able to educate, build relationships, and foster adoption of sound security practices (commitment + compliance).
  • Expert experience with cloud security, platforms and services, including understanding of current security offerings from leading cloud service providers (e.g. AWS, Azure, etc.), and their applicability to securing a SaaS enterprise security environment.
  • Experience in the evaluation and implementation of industry standard enterprise-wide information security technologies and concepts, including but not limited to: SEIM, Application Security, Cloud Security (AWS), Data Loss Prevention, Security Event Management, Threat and Vulnerability Management and Identity and Access Management.
  • Clear understanding of relevant information security governance, technical and security standards and regulations Familiarity with industry security standards and compliances including OWASP, FedRAMP, AICPA SOC, NIST 800-53, 800-171 ISO 27001, CMMC, and ISO 27018 as well as current data privacy regulations, including GDPR and regional standards. Deep knowledge of networking and network security.
  • Strong understanding and experience with Secure SDLC and DevSecOps or security automation Ability to work under pressure across multiple stakeholders.
  • Excellent written and communication skills and ability to communicate across all levels of an organization.

Experience:

description:
At T. Rowe Price, we identify and actively invest in opportunities to help people thrive in an evolving world. As a premier global asset management organization with more than 85 years of experience, we provide investment solutions and a broad range of equity, fixed income, and multi-asset capabilities to individuals, advisors, institutions, and retirement plan sponsors. We take an active, independent approach to investing, offering our dynamic perspective and meaningful partnership so our clients can feel more confident.

We believe doing the right thing for our clients and our associates is good business. With a career at the firm, you can expect opportunities to create real impact at work and in your community. You’ll enjoy resources to support your career path, as well as compensation, benefits, and flexibility to enrich your life. Here, you’ll find a collaborative culture that respects and values differences and colleagues who share a spirit of generosity.

Join us for the opportunity to grow and make a difference in ways that matter to you.

Role Summary

The Analyst, Global Financial Crimes Compliance applies working and conceptual knowledge of fraud and financial crimes investigations to independently manage a range of moderately complex matters. The role is accountable for its own investigative work, coordinates effectively with internal stakeholders, and applies risk-based judgment within established policies, procedures, and escalation frameworks.

This role conducts investigations and inquiries involving suspicious account activity, fraud referrals, alerts, potential account takeover, identity theft, suspicious transactions, financial exploitation indicators, scams, and other financial crime concerns. The role requires the ability to gather and analyze information from multiple internal and external sources, assess the risk implications of the activity, communicate with stakeholders, and maintain complete and defensible investigative documentation.

Responsibilities

  • Research, gather, and evaluate information for escalated alerts, fraud referrals, suspicious activity monitoring cases, and other matters requiring FIU review.
  • Conduct end-to-end investigations of moderate complexity, including review of account activity, transaction history, client or participant interactions, digital activity, documents, internal referrals, and relevant external information.
  • Assess whether activity appears fraudulent, suspicious, inconclusive, or explainable, and document the rationale for recommended disposition.
  • Identify red flags associated with account takeover, identity theft, unauthorized activity, social engineering, scams, financial exploitation, suspicious fund movement, and other financial crime typologies.
  • Prepare clear investigative summaries that include relevant facts, analysis, timelines, findings, recommended actions, and escalation rationale.
  • Determine when matters require escalation to senior investigators, management, Legal, AML, Privacy, Security, business leaders, or other control partners.
  • Support regulatory review considerations, including potential SAR analysis, financial exploitation reporting, law enforcement referral, privacy review, or other required notifications, as applicable.
  • Partner with business, operations, compliance, legal, security, risk, and technology stakeholders to obtain information, resolve open items, and support appropriate risk mitigation.
  • Identify recurring fraud patterns, case themes, process weaknesses, and control gaps observed through investigative work.
  • Contribute to fraud metrics, trend analysis, case categorization, root cause observations, and thematic reviews.
  • Suggest enhancements to monitoring, detection, documentation, procedures, process handoffs, and stakeholder communication.
  • Maintain accurate and complete case records in accordance with policy, procedure, confidentiality expectations, and regulatory standards.
  • Support onboarding, informal peer coaching, knowledge sharing, and team process consistency.

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor's degree or the equivalent combination of education and relevant experience AND
  • 5+ years of total relevant work experience.

Preferred:

  • 2+ years of relevant compliance experience in financial crimes, AML, fraud, or suspicious activity investigations.
  • Strong analytical and investigative skills with the ability to identify suspicious patterns and trends.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including investigative documentation and narrative writing.
  • Sound judgment and ability to make risk-based decisions in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated independence and accountability, with the ability to manage complex investigative work with limited guidance.
  • Familiarity with retail, brokerage, or retirement products.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across multiple groups/levels of management within compliance, legal, operations, and business teams.
  • Ability to meet strict deadlines.
  • Knowledge of BSA/AML, SAR, KYC/CIP, and OFAC requirements.

FINRA Requirements

FINRA licenses are not required and will not be supported for this role.


Work Flexibility

This role is eligible for hybrid work, with up to one day per week from home.

title: Store Collega JD Amsterdam Kalverstraat| 24-32u
description:

  • Je ondersteunt dagelijkse winkelactiviteiten, zoals kassawerkzaamheden, het aanvullen van voorraad, stock room werkzaamheden en het naleven van alle veiligheids- en winkelrichtlijnen.

Wie we zoeken

  • Je hebt een positieve en enthousiaste houding die past binnen een dynamische en klantgerichte retailomgeving.
  • Je beschikt over sterke communicatieve vaardigheden en voelt je comfortabel in het contact met klanten en collega's.

  • Je bent flexibel inzetbaar en bereid om verschillende diensten te werken, waaronder avonden, weekends en drukke seizoensperiodes.

Wat jou extra sterk maakt

title: Mechanical Engineering Leader - Sustaining Engineering
description:
About Us:

BW Papersystems, part of the Barry-Wehmiller Group, builds capital equipment that transforms paper into products for consumers - every day, around the world. We offer innovative technologies, service and parts, and years of global experience in corrugating, finishing; slitting and packaging; stationery; bookbinding and security documents. Customers rely on our machines to produce and convert items such as corrugated boxes, folding cartons, passports, notebooks, copy paper, board, and coated and other specialty papers. For more information, visit bwpapersystems.com.


Barry-Wehmiller is a diversified global supplier of engineering consulting and manufacturing technology for the packaging, corrugating, sheeting and paper-converting industries. By blending people-centric leadership with disciplined operational strategies and purpose-driven growth, Barry-Wehmiller has become a $3 billion organization with nearly 12,000 team members united by a common belief: to use the power of business to build a better world.


Job Description:

The Mechanical Engineering Leader – Sustaining Engineering is responsible for leading the mechanical engineering team that supports released and legacy folding carton product lines. The Sustaining Engineering team owns post-release product support, including issue resolution, product improvements, cost reduction, obsolescence management, and technical support for Operations, Supply Chain, Technical Service, and customers. The team partners with New Product Design Engineering to establish a clear, timely handoff of new products into production and ongoing lifecycle support.

The leader must have a strong understanding of manufacturing operations and communicate effectively with internal and external customers. This role establishes priorities, manages team capacity, and coordinates schedules so sustaining work is completed in line with business needs and agreed-upon deadlines.

The Mechanical Engineering Leader – Sustaining Engineering reports to the Sheboygan Engineering Leader and directs a team of approximately 5–7 mechanical engineering professionals focused on the lifecycle support and continuous improvement of released folding carton machinery.

The role leads engineering response to field and production issues after product release, including structured root-cause analysis, containment, corrective-action design, validation, and implementation. New Product Design Engineering retains ownership of products still in active development until an agreed-upon release and handoff are complete.

This is a key leadership position requiring the ability to translate business priorities into disciplined execution, coordinate cross-functional support, develop engineering capability, and represent the company in customer-facing technical matters.

The leader is responsible for the professional development of the Sustaining Engineering team and for implementing the standards, processes, change controls, and governance needed to support released products and approved customer-specific modifications.

Key Responsibilities:

description:
Torch Technologies

Thank you for your interest in employment with Torch Technologies. We are a 100% employee-owned, Certified Great Place To Work and named Best Places to Work in Huntsville/Madison County, headquartered in Huntsville, AL. Our team provides superior research, development, and engineering services to the Federal Government and Department of War. As one of the nation’s top 100 defense companies, the services we provide directly support the men and women who serve our country. Our corporate mission sums up the pride our employee-owners take in the work we do: “Lighting the Pathway of Freedom”. And, as a Certified Evergreen ESOP, we have made the commitment to grow and sustain our company for the next 100 years! Come grow with us!

Torch Technologies is seeking a highly skilled Chamber Test Analyst to support the 718th Test Squadron (718 TS) at the Arnold Engineering Development Complex (AEDC). The 718 TS operates world-class aerodynamic and propulsion test facilities, and this role is critical to advancing the nation's hypersonic weapon and flight systems. This position is located onsite at Arnold AFB, TN.


As a Test Analyst, your duties will include the following, but are not limited to:


  • Supporting the 718th Test Squadron at the Arnold Engineering Development Complex (AEDC) in the planning, execution, and analysis of testing.
  • Analyzing aerodynamic, thermodynamic, and propulsion data from ground test facilities.
  • Developing comprehensive test plans, test matrices, and safety packages in coordination with facility engineers and program stakeholders.
  • Utilizing data acquisition systems and post-test data reduction tools to evaluate scramjet, ramjet, and other high-speed propulsion system performance.
  • Collaborating with test facility personnel, government customers, and prime contractors to ensure test objectives are safely and effectively met.
  • Generating technical reports, data packages, briefings, and presentations to communicate test results and anomalies to stakeholders.

Required Qualifications:

  • U.S. Citizenship
  • Education - Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a highly related technical field. Additional experience may be substituted for education with customer approval.
  • 3+ years of relevant experience in aeropropulsion, wind tunnel testing, or hypersonic aerodynamics.
  • Proficiency in data analysis and engineering software (e.g., MATLAB, Python, or similar).
  • Familiarity with high-speed/hypersonic propulsion systems and compressible flow dynamics.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex technical data clearly.
  • Must be able to obtain/maintain a Top Secret DoW security clearance. Active clearance must be maintained throughout employment tenure.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a highly related technical field is preferred.
  • Prior experience with AEDC test facilities or the 718th Test Squadron is highly desirable.
