title: Senior Network Engineer {DNS {Infoblox}
description:
About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):

10

About the Role: Senior Network Engineer

The Team: Global Network Services is seeking a Senior Network Engineer to join our dynamic, multi-disciplinary team. You will design, automate, and operate the DNS, edge delivery, and application delivery services that keep S&P Global’s platforms fast, secure, and available. We value continuous learning, excellence, and a proactive mindset.

Responsibilities and Impact

DDI, Edge Security, and Application Delivery

  • Own the architecture and operation of enterprise DDI services, including Infoblox (DNS, DHCP, IPAM) and cloud DNS (AWS Route 53, Azure DNS/Private DNS, Google Cloud DNS), with hybrid DNS resolution across on-premises and multi-cloud environments.
  • Integrate IPAM/DDI with the CMDB to keep IP, host, and network records accurate and in sync, using discovery data and API-driven reconciliation to detect and correct drift.
  • Design and operate DNS security controls, including DNSSEC, DNS firewall (e.g., Infoblox BloxOne Threat Defense), protection against DNS attacks
  • Design and manage CDN, WAF, bot management, and DDoS protection using Akamai and Cloudflare, including rule tuning, policy management, and traffic analysis.
  • Design and operate load balancing and traffic management, including F5, cloud-native load balancers (AWS ELB/ALB, Azure Application Gateway, GCP Load Balancing), and global server load balancing.

Automation and Infrastructure as Code

  • Write, test, and maintain Terraform modules to provision DNS, edge, and load balancing services across AWS, Azure, and GCP, setting shared-module patterns.
  • Build Python tooling and API integrations (e.g., Infoblox WAPI, Akamai ,Cloudflare APIs) to remove repetitive manual tasks and improve consistency.
  • Build and improve CI/CD pipelines for changes, including automated validation, pre-deployment testing, and policy checks.
  • Develop automated configuration and compliance checks to catch deviations from approved standards (e.g., DNS records, WAF policies, IPAM allocations) early.
  • Follow good engineering practice in shared repositories: version control, peer review, modular code, and clear documentation.

Collaboration and Continuous Improvement

  • Serve as subject matter expert and third-line escalation point for complex incidents, leading root cause analysis.
  • Collaborate with application, product, engineering, and security teams to deliver changes meeting enterprise standards and compliance requirements.
  • Plan and execute approved changes within agreed maintenance windows, with documented back-out steps, and join out-of-hours change windows as required.
  • Produce and maintain architecture documentation, automation runbooks, and standard operating procedures.
  • Mentor engineers, share knowledge, and identify ways to reduce risk, improve efficiency, and raise standards.

What We’re Looking For

Basic Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years’ experience in network or infrastructure engineering supporting hybrid, multi-cloud environments.
  • Extensive hands-on experience with Infoblox DDI, including DNS architecture, DHCP, and IPAM design and operations.
  • Hands-on experience with DNS in Infoblox and at least two cloud DNS providers: AWS Route 53, Azure DNS, Google Cloud DNS.
  • Strong experience with Akamai and/or Cloudflare, including CDN, WAF, bot mitigation, and DDoS protection.
  • Hands-on experience with load balancers (e.g., F5, NGINX, AWS ELB/ALB, Akamai GTM).
  • Strong experience with Terraform and Infrastructure as Code, including module design and Git-based version control.
  • Proficiency in Python for automation and API integration, following software development best practices (testing, code review).
  • Solid understanding of core networking, DNS, and HTTP protocols, able to read configuration as code and assess a change’s impact before deploying it.
  • Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills, with attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and the ability to work effectively in a cross-functional team.

Additional Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience querying observability and logging platforms (e.g., Splunk, Grafana , Google Secops etc) to analyze DNS, CDN/WAF, and load balancer telemetry, build dashboards and alerts, and troubleshoot incidents.
  • Experience building AI-assisted automation, such as agents that call Infoblox, Akamai, Cloudflare, or cloud APIs (e.g., via MCP servers).
  • Experience integrating IPAM/DDI with a CMDB or ITSM platform including discovery-based synchronization and automated request workflows.
  • Experience with low-code automation platforms.
  • Active Directory infrastructure knowledge.
  • Experience in a regulated environment with formal change and audit requirements.
  • AI fundamentals.
  • Relevant certifications, such as Infoblox DDI Professional, Terraform Associate, Akamai or Cloudflare certifications, or AWS, Azure, or GCP networking certifications.

title: Senior Manager Strategy
description:
If you’re looking for a special place to build or grow your career, you’ve found it. Whether you’re an experienced professional, a recent college graduate or somewhere in between, IDEX is a place where you can apply your existing skills and learn new ones in an environment where you can make an impact.

With interesting opportunities in engineering, marketing, sales, supply chain, operations, HR, finance, and more across more than 40 diverse businesses around the globe, chances are, we have something special for you.

JOB TITLE: Senior Manager Strategy – IH&S

REPORTS TO: Corey Phipps, VP Business Development

JOB LOCATION: Remote

Who is IDEX Health & Science (IH&S)?

As a business unit of IDEX Corporation, IH&S has a long history of driving growth in life sciences and healthcare by embracing innovation and redefining the supplier-customer relationship. The work we do every day allows us to discover key insights and break new ground to create some of the most meaningful technologies that have a lasting impact on companies, industries, and society.

IDEX HEALTH & SCIENCE, LLC

IDEX Health & Science is the global leader in life science fluidics, microfluidics, and optics, offering a three-fold advantage to customers by bringing optofluidic paths to life with strategic partnerships, solutions, and expertise. As one of the few companies in the world with component, sub-system, and application-level experts, IDEX Health & Science helps instrument developers solve the most demanding fluidic and optical challenges in a wide array of applications. With 1,000 employees around the world, we believe partnership will change the way the world innovates, leading to new technologies that improve our health, protect our planet, and enrich our lives. For more information visit:

Our formula for success is simple. We work hard to maintain a culture where you can own your work; you are encouraged to try new ideas in a collaborative environment; and you can apply your skillset to enable our clients to gain a competitive advantage in their own market. At IDEX Health & Science, you have the opportunity to work with a great group of people, mentor others, and build a great future.

Position Summary

The Senior Manager of Strategy is a hands-on strategy leader and enterprise utility player. This individual helps IH&S make clear choices and convert them into results, combining fact-based strategy formulation with direct ownership of selected execution priorities. The role requires the ability to influence without authority across businesses, functions and geographies.

Reporting to the VP Business Development, the Senior Manager of Strategy formulates and executes the segment strategy, supports portfolio and resource-allocation choices, and accelerates a focused set of organic and inorganic growth priorities. This person works closely with the GMs of optics & fluidics businesses, commercial leaders, Finance, Corporate Development, and functional partners.

This is a builder-doer role and is expected to develop the market-backed point of view, build the business case, align stakeholders, create the workplan, and remain involved through implementation. Success depends less on formal authority and more on analytical credibility, sound judgment, strong relationships, and consistent follow-through.

What’s Unique and Exciting About this Role:

  • Entrepreneurial environment with strategy as a critical role.
  • Opportunity to shape where IH&S plays, how it wins and how resources are deployed.
  • Direct ownership of strategy work products and selected execution priorities.
  • Broad exposure across markets, customers, technologies, businesses and enterprise leaders.
  • High autonomy in a matrixed environment, with impact created through influence, facts and follow-through.
  • Utility-player mandate spanning market analysis, executive alignment, initiative leadership, M&A support and operating cadence.

Key Responsibilities

  • Formulate differentiated strategies. Develop fact-based segment, platform and business strategies, in collaboration with the VP GMs for each business, grounded in market, customer, competitor, technology and financial insight. Translate analysis into explicit where-to-play, how-to-win, capability, and resource-allocation of choices.

  • Turn strategy into execution. Convert strategic priorities into sequenced workplans, accountable owners, milestones, KPIs, and value targets. Personally lead selected cross-business initiatives from definition through implementation rather than handing off the work after the recommendation.
  • Drive cross-business growth. Identify and advance opportunities that can drive growth for IH&S through connected capabilities across HST, channel access, customer relationships, or coordinated commercial action. Build the case, align stakeholders, resolve barriers, and maintain momentum.
  • Support portfolio and M&A decisions. Shape target themes, screen opportunities, develop strategic rationales and business cases, and partner with Corporate Development and business leaders through cultivation, diligence, deal evaluation and integration planning.
  • Build external and competitive insights. Create a practical market-intelligence rhythm that identifies shifts in customer needs, technology, competition, regulation, and capital deployment. Distill implications for leadership decisions and strategic priorities to share externally with investor community
  • Establish performance visibility. Define leading and lagging indicators for top strategic initiatives. Build simple mechanisms to track value creation, surface gaps early, and drive corrective action.
  • Enable leadership decisions. Structure ambiguous questions, develop decision-ready options, and facilitate productive debate. Prepare clear executive narratives, presentations, and recommendations for segment and enterprise leadership.

  • Strengthen strategic capability. Develop reusable tools, standard work and problem-solving approaches that improve strategic thinking and execution across IH&S. Coach teams through the work while remaining directly engaged in the analysis and output.
  • Serve as a utility player. Step into critical, time-sensitive work that may not fit neatly within one function. Rapidly learn about the issue, create structure, mobilize the right people, and deliver a practical outcome.

How Success Will Be Measured

  • Quality, clarity and adoption of IH&S strategic choices across businesses and functions.
  • Measurable revenue, margin, cash or enterprise-value impact from initiatives personally led or enabled.
  • Speed and quality of execution against agreed milestones, with risks surfaced and resolved early.
  • Strength and strategic fit of the organic and inorganic growth pipeline.
  • Effectiveness in aligning stakeholders and advancing work without relying on formal authority.
  • Improved strategic capability, standard work and decision quality across the segment.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in business, Engineering, Economics, Science or a related field; MBA or relevant advanced degree preferred.
  • Approximately 8–12+ years of progressive experience in strategy, general management, commercial leadership, corporate development, transformation, or a related role.
  • Demonstrated experience both formulating strategy and executing it through measurable business outcomes.
  • Background in health and science technology, health and science markets, manufacturing or another complex B2B environment strongly preferred.
  • Experience in a top-tier strategy consulting environment and/or a high-impact corporate strategy role is helpful but must be paired with evidence of hands-on implementation.
  • Experience building market-backed growth strategies, business cases, and executive recommendations using financial, commercial and operational data.
  • Working knowledge of M&A strategy, target assessment, diligence and integration planning; direct transaction experience is a plus.
  • ·Track record of influencing senior leaders and cross-functional teams in a matrixed, global organization without direct reporting authority.

Attributes & Skills

  • Doer first: rolls up sleeves, builds the analysis, drafts the recommendation and stays involved through implementation.
  • Utility player who moves easily across strategic, commercial, financial, operational and organizational questions.
  • Influencer without authority who builds alignment through facts, trust, listening and clear trade-offs.
  • Strategy-to-results operator who connects long-term direction to near-term actions, owners, milestones and economics.
  • Structured problem solver who simplifies complexity and separates signal from noise.
  • Commercially and financially fluent, with a practical understanding of markets, customer value, margins, returns and risk.
  • Low ego and high accountability; shares credit, invites challenge and takes ownership for outcomes.
  • Clear, concise communicator who produces decision-ready narratives for business teams and senior executives.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity and able to create direction as facts evolve.
  • Curious and externally oriented, with the ability to find and evaluate credible market intelligence.

What This Role Is Not

  • A staff role focused only on presentations, annual planning or coordinating others’ work.
  • A pure advisory position that ends when the recommendation is delivered.
  • A role that depends on positional authority to create action.
  • A narrowly defined functional job; priorities will shift as the business and strategy evolve.

Rithum expects employees across all roles to leverage AI and technology to improve efficiency, streamline workflows, and create scalable ways of working.

Rithum is embedding AI into every corner of how it operates — and security is no exception.

As a Staff Information Security Engineer, you own the intersection of AI adoption and information security: designing guardrails for AI-powered products, building automated security tooling, designing security controls and monitoring for an AI-First workforce, helping every team at Rithum move fast without creating risk they cannot see. This is not a typical security role. You spend as much time building and automating as you do reviewing, turning a repeating control into infrastructure-as-code, a manual review into a workflow, and a vague AI risk into a concrete, enforced guardrails. You work autonomously, balancing research with fast-paced delivery, and collaborating closely with Platform Engineering, IT, Security Champions, and external auditors.

Responsibilities

  • Act as the bridge between architectural intent and operational reality; mediate conflicts between security requirements and feasible implementation, propose compensating controls where gaps exist and help register, track and remediate residual risks.
  • Implement preventive, default-on security controls across cloud and enterprise environments, codified as policy- and infrastructure-as-code so security is enforced by design, including controls that govern how AI tools and models may be used.
  • Implement and enforce identity and access controls to an agreed standard, including access boundaries for AI systems and non-human/agent identities by partnering with Platform Engineering and IT to align tooling and policy to the architecture.
  • Assist in maintaining the InfoSec risk register; track emerging threats and translate them into actionable guidance for engineering teams.
  • Support third-party and vendor risk assessments, with a focus on vendors who process data through AI pipelines.
  • Automate repetitive security workflows (evidence collection, access reviews, alert enrichment) and build or operate AI-assisted security agents — with human-in-the-loop approval gates, least-privilege credentials, and explicit attention to each agent's own blast radius.
  • Integrate security tooling (SIEM, CSPM, DAST/SAST, vulnerability scanners) with LLM layers to surface actionable insight and automated responses.
  • Define and enforce security requirements for AI-powered features: model access controls, prompt-injection mitigations, output validation, and data-handling boundaries.
  • Conduct threat modelling on agentic and LLM-based systems, accounting for novel attack surfaces such as tool misuse, indirect prompt injection, and supply chain risk.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

  • 5+ years of security engineering experience with demonstrated AI/ML security depth (prompt injection, model supply chain, adversarial inputs, RAG).
  • Experience using AI tools (ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude, etc.) and LLM frameworks and APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, or similar) to accelerate and elevate your work.
  • Hands-on identity and access expertise across modern enterprise and cloud identity stacks, including access models for AI systems and non-human identities.
  • Infrastructure and policy-as-code (e.g. Terraform, OPA/Rego) and proficiency in a scripting language for automation (Python preferred).
  • Cloud security expertise: AWS Solutions Architect / Security Specialty or equivalent demonstrated expertise, including multi-account governance, preventive guardrails, and policy-as-code.
  • Application security (OWASP Top 10 and the OWASP LLM/GenAI Top 10, secure SDLC) and threat-modelling methodologies (STRIDE, PASTA, or equivalent). Practical experience building or operating AI agents, and integrating security tooling (SIEM, CSPM, SAST/DAST/SCA) so it surfaces action rather than raw alerts.
  • Working knowledge of SOC 2 and/or ISO 27001 control frameworks.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building or operating AI agents in a production environment.
  • Awareness of privacy regulation (GDPR/CCPA) as it touches AI including privacy-by-design and DPIAs.
  • Red teaming or adversarial ML research backgrounds.
  • Experience implementing privileged-access, key-management, posture-management, or data-protection programs.
  • Experience with EDR, CASB, DLP, Security automation and SAST, DAST, IAST and SCA tools.
  • Cloud Architecture or Security certifications (CCSK, TAISE, AWS).

Travel Required
Up to 10%

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

What it’s like to work at Rithum

When you join Rithum, you can expect to work with smart risk-takers, courageous collaborators, and curious minds.

As part of the Rithum team, you are valued, supported, and included. Guided by a transparent culture and accessible, approachable leadership, we offer career opportunities aligned to your ambitions and talents. Final compensation may vary depending on geographic location, skills, and relevant experience.In addition to base pay, we offer a discretionary bonus for non-sales roles, a comprehensive benefits package, and, where applicable, sales incentives.

Looking for a role where you’ll be at the heart of every successful departure? Ramp Agents at Southwest work outside to guide planes, move bags and cargo, help with de-icing planes during cold weather, and help keep our operation running smoothly. Additional details

  • This is a part-time opportunity. At Southwest, Part-Time Employees generally work 32 hours over 5 days, but schedules are determined in accordance with a seniority-based bidding process.
  • New Hires will complete 4-6 weeks of training. Training will consist of 8-hours of classroom or on-the-job training over 5 days each week.
  • After completing training, Part-Time New Hire work weeks will consist of 6.5-hour shifts over 5 days, with the potential for mandatory overtime.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Provide friendly service to and maintains positive relationships with all internal and external Customers

  • Receive and record Customer baggage, air freight, mail and company materials as required

Submits, either electronically or manually, a Cargo Bin Loading Slip (CBLS) to an Operations Agent

  • Operate and/or drive motorized equipment, such as belt loaders, air start units, lift trucks, push back tugs, bag cart, lavatory cart and de-icers
  • Manually pushes and pulls push carts and containers
  • Work in the vicinity of and between passenger terminals, hangars and airfreight facilities, both indoors and outdoors
  • May be exposed to a wide variety of weather condition, jet and machinery noises, fumes, dirt and dust for extended periods of time
  • Completes forms and paperwork connected with work assignments according to established procedures, and enters such information in to the Company’s information system as required
  • Duties vary by size and organization of station.
  • Provide friendly service to all Co-workers and Customers. Has routine contact with people outside of the Company such as delivery agents, shippers, etc.
  • Must be able to meet any physical ability requirements listed on this description
  • May perform other job duties as directed by Employee's Leaders

Knowledge, Skills and Responsibilities

  • Ability to work well with others as part of a team, and work under stressful situations
  • Must be able to satisfactorily complete Ramp Agent training program with a 90% or greater average and an evaluation period
  • Ability to read documents, follow instructions, learn and understand ramp operations procedures, rules and regulations
  • Must be aware of hazardous situations and be able to handle emergencies as needed
  • Must work under tight time constraints to accomplish quick turns of aircraft
  • Must meet all grooming standards as outlined in the Ground Operations Employee Handbook and the Labor Agreement
  • Must be able to be alert to moving vehicles or aircraft and use radio equipment. Must be able to communicate information and instructions verbally and/or via radio equipment

Education

  • No education requirement

Experience

  • No experience requirement

Licensing/Certification

  • Must possess a valid state motor vehicle operator's license
  • Must be able to obtain a SIDA badge and meet all local airport requirements
  • May be required by Station Leadership to obtain a Customs Seal and meet all requirements to work international flights

Physical Abilities

  • Must be able to lift and move items of 70 pounds and/or more on a regular basis and repetitively lift weights of 40 to 50 pounds on raised surfaces
  • Must be able to climb, bend, kneel, crawl, and stoop on a frequent basis and for extended periods
  • Must be able to work in cramped or high places
  • Must be able to carry heavy items up and down jetway stairs
  • Must maintain the ability to wear prescribed uniforms

Other Qualifications

  • Must maintain a well-groomed appearance per Company appearance standards as described in established guidelines
  • Must be a U.S. citizen or have authorization to work in the United States as defined by the Immigration Reform Act of 1986
  • Must be at least 18 years of age
  • Must be able to comply with Company attendance standards as described in established guidelines
  • Ability to work shift work and/or overtime

title: Hypersonic Aeropropulsion Test Analyst
description:
Torch Technologies

Thank you for your interest in employment with Torch Technologies. We are a 100% employee-owned, Certified Great Place To Work and named Best Places to Work in Huntsville/Madison County, headquartered in Huntsville, AL. Our team provides superior research, development, and engineering services to the Federal Government and Department of War. As one of the nation’s top 100 defense companies, the services we provide directly support the men and women who serve our country. Our corporate mission sums up the pride our employee-owners take in the work we do: “Lighting the Pathway of Freedom”. And, as a Certified Evergreen ESOP, we have made the commitment to grow and sustain our company for the next 100 years! Come grow with us!

Torch Technologies is seeking a highly skilled Hypersonic Aeropropulsion Test Analyst to support the 715th Test Squadron (715 TS) at the Arnold Engineering Development Complex (AEDC). The 715 TS operates world-class aerodynamic and propulsion test facilities, and this role is critical to advancing the nation's hypersonic weapon and flight systems. This position is located onsite at Arnold AFB, TN.


As a Test Analyst, your duties will include the following, but are not limited to:


  • Supporting the 715th Test Squadron at the Arnold Engineering Development Complex (AEDC) in the planning, execution, and analysis of hypersonic aeropropulsion ground testing.
  • Analyzing aerodynamic, thermodynamic, and propulsion data from ground test facilities (such as the Aerodynamic and Propulsion Test Unit - APTU).
  • Developing comprehensive test plans, test matrices, and safety packages in coordination with facility engineers and program stakeholders.
  • Utilizing data acquisition systems and post-test data reduction tools to evaluate scramjet, ramjet, and other high-speed propulsion system performance.
  • Collaborating with test facility personnel, government customers, and prime contractors to ensure test objectives are safely and effectively met.
  • Generating technical reports, data packages, briefings, and presentations to communicate test results and anomalies to stakeholders.

Required Qualifications:

  • U.S. Citizenship
  • Education - Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a highly related technical field. Additional experience may be substituted for education with customer approval.
  • Proficiency in data analysis and engineering software (e.g., MATLAB, Python, or similar).
  • Familiarity with high-speed/hypersonic propulsion systems and compressible flow dynamics.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex technical data clearly.
  • Must be able to obtain/maintain Secret DoW security clearance. Active clearance must be maintained throughout employment tenure.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a highly related technical field is preferred.
  • 3+ years of relevant experience in aeropropulsion, wind tunnel testing, or hypersonic aerodynamics.
  • Prior experience with AEDC test facilities or the 715th Test Squadron is highly desirable.

title: Sr. Collaboration Systems Administrator
description:
Meet the Moment with Alteryx

We're living through a once-in-a-generation shift in how work gets done. Data, automation, and AI are quickly becoming the center of every business decision - and Alteryx is leading the transformation.

You'll be working on the challenges that sit at the heart of modern business. No matter your role, the work you do will help organizations move faster, see more clearly, and tackle questions that used to feel impossible.

If you're ready to meet the moment with innovation, curiosity, and excellence, there's a place for you here.

We are on a mission to radically improve how our employees interact with IT and business services. Reporting directly to the Sr. Director, End User Services, you will be the technical owner and primary advocate for the collaboration and support platforms that drive our employees’ daily productivity—including our employee service/ticketing/virtual agent ecosystem, Slack, Jira, Confluence, and more.

This is a senior technical, hands-on role that serves as a key pillar of our broader End User Services team. You will work in tight alignment with end-user support, system operations, and other IT and business functions to drive the ongoing administration, enablement, and strategic enhancement of these systems.

We are seeking a forward-thinking, innovative technologist who cares deeply about the end-user journey. You will serve as the central point of intake for platform enhancement requests, developing roadmaps that anticipate requirements and ensure our tools exceed employee needs before a problem is ever brought forward. You will have ownership of the digital workplace experience, designing consumer-grade self-service experiences, deploying AI and automation, and eliminating friction across all platforms—while balancing this drive for employee satisfaction with the discipline to ensure our ecosystem remains governed, auditable, reportable, and accountable.


Key Duties and Expectations

  • Holistic Platform Administration & Ownership: Serve as the primary technical administrator and subject matter expert for our core employee technology stack (Slack, ESM/Ticketing, Virtual Agents, Jira, Confluence, DocuSign, etc.).
  • Proactive Enhancement & Intake Management: Act as the central hub for platform enhancement requests. Analyze support trends, usage data, and business feedback to anticipate future needs, driving an ongoing roadmap that evolves these platforms to exceed employee expectations proactively.
  • Employee-Centric Workflow & Enablement: Build intuitive workflows, communication channels, and service requests. Partner with cross-functional teams to drive enablement, stripping away legacy complexities to design processes that prioritize speed, simplicity, and seamless collaboration.
  • Next-Gen Self-Service & AI: Think beyond the traditional IT ticket. Deploy and optimize virtual agents (e.g., within Slack), AI-driven knowledge bases, and smart automation to enable "zero-touch" resolutions and empower users to confidently solve their own problems.
  • Integrations & Automation: Build and maintain seamless integrations (via REST APIs, webhooks, native hubs, etc.) connecting our suite of tools (Slack, Jumpcloud, Workday, Jira, etc.) to automate user lifecycles, support tasks, and cross-platform workflows.
  • Governance & Accountability: Establish a well-organized system of record. Ensure that while the front-end user experience is effortless, the back-end data architecture provides strict audibility, clear accountability, and robust reporting for leadership and compliance teams.
  • Asset Accountability (ITAM): Configure hardware and software asset management capabilities to ensure accurate tracking, lifecycle management, and financial accountability without bogging down the business in red tape.

Experience & Education Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Administration, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5 or more years of hands-on experience administering enterprise collaboration, workflow, and ESM platforms (e.g., Slack Enterprise Grid, Jira/Confluence, DocuSign, Freshservice, ServiceNow, Zendesk, etc.) with a strong portfolio of projects focused on improving user experience.
  • Administration certifications in modern SaaS platforms (Slack, Atlassian, ESM platforms) are a strong plus. Note: A conceptual understanding of traditional ITSM frameworks (like ITIL) is helpful for context, but we are looking for an agile, employee-first mindset over strict framework compliance.
  • Proven track record of implementing self-service portals, automated routing, and/or chatbots.
  • Experience managing platform integrations using REST APIs, webhooks, and JSON.
  • Experience designing reporting dashboards and ensuring system data meets audit and compliance standards.

Required Skills

  • UX & Innovation Mindset: A passion for "outside-the-box" problem solving. You treat employees as customers and design technology solutions that they actually want to use.
  • Data & Governance Discipline: Ability to plan and build systems that are easily reportable, structurally sound, and compliant with audit requirements.
  • Integration & Scripting: Proficiency in interacting with REST/SOAP APIs and basic scripting capability (e.g., JavaScript, Python, or PowerShell) to automate the mundane and connect disparate systems.
  • Systems Simplification: The ability to look at a tangled legacy process, extract the actual business requirement, and rebuild it in the simplest way possible.
  • Communication: Exceptional ability to collaborate with non-technical stakeholders, gather feedback, and translate it into technical action.

title: RADIAC Test Engineer (TOC)
description:
Torch Technologies

Thank you for your interest in employment with Torch Technologies. We are a 100% employee-owned, Certified Great Place To Work and named Best Places to Work in Huntsville/Madison County, headquartered in Huntsville, AL. Our team provides superior research, development, and engineering services to the Federal Government and Department of War. As one of the nation’s top 100 defense companies, the services we provide directly support the men and women who serve our country. Our corporate mission sums up the pride our employee-owners take in the work we do: “Lighting the Pathway of Freedom”. And, as a Certified Evergreen ESOP, we have made the commitment to grow and sustain our company for the next 100 years! Come grow with us!

Torch Technologies Inc., is seeking a Temporary On-Call (TOC) RADIAC Test Engineer to support U.S. Army Radiation Detection, Indication, and Computation (RADIAC) systems. The ideal candidate will provide technical expertise in the evaluation of radiation detection equipment performance characteristics, assist in the development and validation of calibration procedures, and support software-based testing and analysis capabilities. This position requires the candidate to have a strong understanding of radiation detection principles, electronic instrumentation, and equipment testing and calibration. The candidate will collaborate with government personnel, engineers, and technicians to improve testing methodologies, calibration processes, and overall equipment performance. This position is remote, with work performed on an as-needed basis.

As a RADIAC Test Engineer (TOC), your duties will include but are not limited to the following technical responsibilities outlined below.

  • Provide technical expertise and recommendations regarding the performance characteristics, capabilities, limitations, and operational requirements of U.S. Army RADIAC equipment.
  • Evaluate radiation detection instrumentation to assess measurement accuracy, sensitivity, response characteristics, repeatability, and overall system performance.
  • Assist in the development, evaluation, and validation of calibration procedures for radiation detection and measurement equipment.
  • Support the identification of appropriate test methods, calibration instrumentation, acceptance criteria, and measurement techniques.
  • Analyze equipment specifications, technical documentation, and test results to identify performance deficiencies and recommend improvements.
  • Support the development and implementation of software-based tools for automated testing, calibration, data acquisition, and analysis.
  • Collaborate with software engineers to define technical requirements and support the integration of instrumentation with software applications.
  • Provide troubleshooting and technical support for radiation detection equipment, electronic instrumentation, and associated test systems.
  • Develop, review, and maintain technical procedures, test documentation, calibration instructions, and engineering reports.
  • Utilize strong organizational and communication skills to collaborate with government stakeholders, engineering teams, and other technical personnel.

Required Qualifications:

  • U.S. Citizenship.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Nuclear Engineering, Physics, Electrical Engineering, Engineering Technology, or a related technical discipline with 5+ years of relevant experience in nuclear systems, radiation detection, electronic instrumentation, equipment testing, or related technical fields.
  • OR Master’s degree in Nuclear Engineering, Physics, Electrical Engineering, Engineering Technology, or a related technical discipline with 3+ years of relevant experience in nuclear systems, radiation detection, electronic instrumentation, equipment testing, or related technical fields.
  • Understanding of radiation detection principles, nuclear instrumentation, and measurement system performance.
  • Experience with testing, troubleshooting, maintenance, or calibration of electronic instrumentation or complex technical systems.
  • Ability to interpret technical specifications, evaluate equipment performance, and provide technical recommendations.
  • Experience developing, reviewing, or implementing technical procedures, test documentation, or equipment maintenance instructions.
  • Familiarity with computer-based technical applications and software used in testing, measurement, data collection, or analysis.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, technical writing, and communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary engineering teams.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree or higher in Nuclear Engineering, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline with 5+ years of relevant experience in nuclear systems, radiation detection, electronic instrumentation, equipment testing, or related technical fields.
  • Experience in the research, development, characterization, or evaluation of radiation detection instrumentation.
  • Experience with scintillation detectors, neutron detection, gamma radiation measurement, or other radiation measurement technologies.
  • Experience performing calibration, characterization, or performance evaluations of nuclear instrumentation and radiation detection equipment.
  • Experience with neutron radiography, nondestructive testing, or nuclear research laboratory operations.
  • Experience with U.S. Army RADIAC equipment or other military radiation detection systems.
  • Familiarity with automated test equipment, software-based instrument control, data acquisition systems, or calibration software.
  • Experience with programming, scripting, or software development tools used for instrumentation control, test automation, or data analysis.
  • Experience with nuclear instrumentation and control systems, electronic equipment maintenance, or component-level troubleshooting.
  • Experience developing technical manuals, calibration procedures, maintenance instructions, or standardized test procedures.

title: Senior Network Security Engineer
description:
SWBC is seeking an experienced Senior Network Security Engineer to design, implement, operate, and improve enterprise network security controls across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments. This position owns or supports major network security platforms and capabilities, including firewalls, segmentation, VPNs, secure cloud connectivity, intrusion prevention, and network security telemetry.

The Senior Network Security Engineer collaborates with Network Operations, Cloud Operations, Security Operations, infrastructure, application, and development teams to provide secure and resilient connectivity across the enterprise. The role requires strong hands-on experience with Palo Alto Networks and Cisco firewalls, enterprise routing, AWS and Microsoft Azure networking, production change control, and complex incident resolution.

Why you’ll love this role:

This role is ideal for an experienced network security professional who enjoys solving complex technical challenges and shaping secure, resilient enterprise connectivity. You will have the opportunity to own critical security platforms, influence hybrid-cloud architecture, lead major changes and incident resolution, mentor technical team members, and strengthen security across SWBC’s enterprise environment.

Essential duties include the following:


  • Design, implement, operate, and improve secure enterprise network architectures across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments.
  • Deploy, configure, manage, and troubleshoot Palo Alto Networks and Cisco firewalls, including security policies, NAT policies, security zones, objects, application controls, and access-control policies.
  • Design and implement network segmentation, micro-segmentation, and isolation controls to reduce attack surfaces and limit lateral movement.
  • Perform firewall migrations, upgrades, configuration changes, policy optimization, and complex troubleshooting.
  • Develop and maintain network security standards, architecture documentation, network diagrams, implementation procedures, and operational runbooks.
  • Design, implement, and troubleshoot remote-access VPN solutions and site-to-site IPsec tunnels, including authentication, encryption, routing, and tunnel connectivity.
  • Establish secure connectivity among corporate offices, data centers, cloud environments, remote users, and third-party organizations.
  • Design, implement, and troubleshoot enterprise routing architectures, including BGP, OSPF, route redistribution, route filtering, route summarization, and routing policies.
  • Apply strong knowledge of TCP/IP, subnetting, VLANs, NAT, DNS, DHCP, network segmentation, high availability, and redundancy.
  • Design and implement secure AWS VPC and Microsoft Azure VNet architectures, including subnets, route tables, network security controls, and hybrid connectivity.
  • Evaluate cloud network architectures and configurations for security risks, misconfigurations, and control gaps and support cloud transformation initiatives.
  • Configure and maintain IDS/IPS, firewall logging, and network security telemetry and coordinate integration into centralized monitoring and incident-response workflows.
  • Serve as a senior technical resolver for complex network security incidents and service disruptions and lead or contribute to root-cause analysis and corrective actions.
  • Participate in the defined on-call rotation and support major technical escalations.
  • Support compliance and audit activities by maintaining controls, producing audit-ready evidence, and coordinating remediation related to PCI DSS, SOC 2, NIST, ISO 27001, and other applicable requirements.
  • Own assigned network security platforms or major subsystems throughout their operational lifecycle.
  • Plan, sponsor, present, test, validate, implement, and review non-trivial production changes through established change-control processes, including appropriate rollback plans.
  • Coordinate remediation of vulnerabilities affecting firewalls, VPN services, network appliances, edge controls, and cloud network infrastructure.
  • Support disaster recovery planning and testing for assigned network security platforms and services.
  • Use operational metrics to improve service reliability, change quality, vulnerability remediation, and incident resolution.
  • Maintain complete and accurate change, incident, problem, vulnerability, and technical evidence records in ServiceNow or other approved systems.
  • Collaborate with technical teams, translate security requirements into practical solutions, and provide guidance for network, cloud connectivity, infrastructure, and application architecture decisions.
  • Mentor analysts, administrators, and engineers and provide technical guidance during complex changes and incidents.
  • Communicate complex technical and security concepts effectively to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Support Security Assurance and Governance, Risk, and Compliance activities through technical evidence, control validation, and remediation support.
  • Perform all other duties as assigned.

Serious candidates will possess the minimum qualifications:


  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Minimum of seven (7) years of experience in network engineering, network security, cloud network security, infrastructure security, or a combination of these areas.
  • Extensive experience designing, implementing, securing, and supporting enterprise network environments.
  • Extensive hands-on experience with Palo Alto Networks firewalls and hands-on experience with Cisco firewalls, including Cisco ASA or Cisco Secure Firewall/FTD.
  • Strong experience with remote-access VPN and site-to-site IPsec VPN technologies.
  • Strong understanding of enterprise routing concepts, including BGP and OSPF.
  • Hands-on experience with routing, network security, and hybrid connectivity in AWS and Microsoft Azure.
  • Strong knowledge of TCP/IP, VLANs, subnetting, NAT, network segmentation, DNS, DHCP, defense-in-depth, and network security architecture.
  • Experience implementing production changes through formal change-control processes, including testing, validation, rollback planning, and documentation.
  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot and resolve complex technical incidents beyond established runbooks and contribute to root-cause analysis, corrective actions, vulnerability remediation, and recurrence reduction.
  • Experience creating technical standards, architecture diagrams, implementation procedures, automation, or design documentation.
  • Knowledge of IDS/IPS, firewall logging, network security monitoring, SIEM integration, and related telemetry.
  • Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code and automation technologies such as Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible, Python, or PowerShell.
  • Working knowledge of security standards and control frameworks applicable to network and cloud security.
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, documentation, problem-solving, written communication, and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, evolving environment and participate in defined on-call responsibilities as a senior technical resolver.
  • Current Cisco CCNP, preferably CCNP Enterprise or an equivalent certification, or Palo Alto Networks Certified Network Security Engineer (PCNSE) certification.
  • AWS Certified Advanced Networking – Specialty, AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional, a relevant Microsoft Azure network or security certification, CISSP, or an equivalent advanced security certification is preferred.
  • Experience working in financial services or another regulated industry is preferred.

SWBC offers*:

  • Competitive overall compensation package

  • Employee engagement activities and recognition awards
  • Years of Service awards
  • Career enhancement and growth opportunities
  • Leadership Academy and Mentor Program
  • Continuing education and career certifications

  • Lucrative Wellness Program

*Based upon employee eligibility

SWBC is a Substance-Free Workplace and requires pre-employment drug testing.

Please note, SWBC does not hire tobacco users as allowed by law.

title: Seasonal Operations Representative: Orlando, FL
description:
Company Introduction

WorldStrides is the global leader in educational travel and experiential learning. The company was founded in 1967 to provide middle school travel programs to Washington, D.C. and has grown to provide a wide range of programs for more than half a million students annually to over 100 countries around the world. WorldStrides offers experiential learning programs in educational travel, performing arts, language immersion, career exploration, service-learning, study abroad, and sports. Each of these experiences helps students to see beyond the classroom and to see the world – and themselves – in new ways.

Job Description:

World Class Vacations by WorldStrides is a leader in student group travel and experiences. Hundreds of groups have trusted that we will deliver a safe, comprehensive, and educational experience. The Orlando Operations Team of World Class Vacations by WorldStrides, are responsible for the successful implementation of group itineraries as assigned. From the time the group arrives at the Orlando International Airport, to the time the group leaves, our team is in constant communication with the groups and acts as the main point-of-contact for Group Leaders. By providing an organized and easy travel experience, group leaders and students can focus on having fun during their trip. This is a seasonal part-time position with a variety of shifts between February and June 30th. There are no set hours for this position but rather shifts that reflect the needs of the company and the volume of groups traveling at any given time.

Responsibilities:

The Orlando Operations Representative reports to the Destination Operations Coordinator and Manager and is responsible for the facilitation of:

  • Group Resort Check-In and Check-Out
  • Hospitality Room Set-Up
  • Special Events (ex. Pizza Parties, Group Dinners, Special Ticketed Events, etc.)
  • Bus Move Operations
  • Daily Group “Float and Promote”
  • Luggage Pick-Up/Drop-Off
  • Team Communication
  • Other duties as assigned

Qualifications:

  • Must have availability during peak times - February through June.
  • Team player that works well with students, teachers, local vendors, and WorldStrides staff.
  • Ability to navigate a group through the city by foot and metro efficiently.
  • Time management and organizational skills.
  • Integrity and responsibility.
  • Passion for helping others.
  • Excellent customer service and communication skills.
  • Experience working with student populations preferred.
  • Critical thinking and creative problem-solving skills.
  • Skilled at multitasking and able to work with minimal supervision.
  • Basic fundamental computer literacy/skills.
  • Access to a reliable personal vehicle for occasional use.
  • Able to remain on your feet for assigned shifts and to lift and/or move up to 30 pounds when assisting travelers with luggage.

Perks at Work:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Mileage reimbursement (when applicable)

WorldStrides, a global organization, is committed to educate and serve communities worldwide. Our commitment is fueled by the passion of our team members and partners to make experiential learning accessible, while also being socially, environmentally, and ethically responsible. Together, we accomplish this by investing in initiatives to promote inclusion, diversity, and sustainability.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, WorldStrides is committed to building a diverse workforce, supported by an environment that promotes inclusion and belonging. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

WorldStrides will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States. This is not a position for which sponsorship will be provided. Individuals with temporary visas such as E, F-1, J-1, H-1, H-2, L, B, J or TN, or who need sponsorship for work authorization now or in the future, are not eligible for hire. Select seasonal roles may consider students on J-1 or F-1 visas.

title: Therapeutic Coach - START
location: San Jose - 2107 North First St - Suite 655
description:
If you are a current YAI employee, please click this link to apply through your Workday account.


Key/Essential Functions & Responsibilities:


  • Supports individuals across assigned region(s) temporarily accessing crisis or planned services, implementing person-centered therapeutic interventions within their homes and across a variety of community settings including schools, hospitals or group homes and working with primary caregivers and circles of support to successfully implement these interventions and strategies to mitigate crisis or de-escalate behaviors while maintaining professional boundaries and following all applicable guidelines.
  • Conducts regular coaching visits and observational assessments, providing feedback to START team about biopsychosocial factors influencing current functioning, effects of interventions and coaching outcomes.
  • Participates in the identification and development of creative, appropriate therapeutic interventions and strategies based on individual needs for persons supported across assigned region(s) with a focus on positive psychology and stabilization and consideration of persons’ strengths, skills and interests.
  • Plans, structures and prompts social and leisure time activities for persons supported during coaching sessions, including activities that build skills for positive supports, stress reduction, health and wellness, communication, adaptive and/or daily living.
  • Assists individuals with successfully implementing strategies and completing daily activities, personal care, behavioral health needs and health, wellness and/or leisure activities within their homes or in the community.
  • Provides consultation and hands-on education relating to therapeutic interventions, crisis stabilization and prevention for persons supported and their circles of support to create a safe, nurturing and meaningful home environment, using effective teaching methods.
  • Secures and maintains appropriate recreational supplies for therapeutic interventions, scheduling use when necessary and transporting supplies to and from coaching sessions.
  • Participates in development and implementation of Cross-Systems Crisis Prevention and Intervention Plans for persons supported, communicating responses to therapeutic coaching and interventions to support evaluation of progress and updates to plans or interventions.
  • Participates in recurring consultation, staff and other meetings with START leadership, clinical team and START Therapeutic Coaching program.
  • Maintains appropriate communication with persons supported, their caregivers, circles of support and other external parties (e.g. community, providers, etc.) to provide information, receive updates and enhance services and linkages.
  • Completes and maintains all applicable documentation, paperwork and/or records, including resolution of concerns and reporting of incidents relating to assigned caseload.
  • Accurately enters all required data into START Information Reporting System and other appropriate systems, as required by state, on a timely and contemporaneous basis.
  • Responds appropriately to individual safety needs, including reporting significant changes in behavior and health in accordance with all requirements and escalates to clinical team and/or START leadership, when needed.
  • Conducts regular outreach with community partners to maintain linkages and relationships.
  • Completes and maintains all necessary trainings based on assigned program/region to ensure compliance with YAI policies, NCSS and applicable state regulatory agency (e.g. OPWDD, DDS, DDD) requirements.
  • Complies with all Federal, State, Local and other relevant regulatory agency requirements, including the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).
  • Performs all other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualification Requirements including education, experience, licensure/certification, etc. and essential physical capabilities (e.g., lifting, assisting lifting, standing, etc.)

  • Bachelor's degree in psychology, social work or other human services field; and
  • At least two (2) years of experience working with the I/DD population and/or behavioral health needs; or
  • Satisfactory combination of education, experience and/or training as authorized by START/NCSS and/or appropriate State regulatory agency (e.g. OPWDD, etc.).
  • Highly flexible and creative, with the ability to incorporate personal interests, skills and strengths in the creation and implementation of impactful and engaging therapeutic activities or strategies for each individual.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within START team and with people at all levels outside of the organization, including caregivers and circles of support.
  • Independent and organized with a willingness to take initiative.
  • Strong time management skills, including the ability to appropriately prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment to meet prescribed timelines and caseload needs.
  • Ability to travel regularly across assigned region(s) to conduct in-person coaching sessions and visits as required by caseload and/or to facilitate discharges, which may include weekends and/or evenings for assignments in New York.
  • Valid Driver's License required for California and New Jersey assignments; strongly preferred for assignments in New York, especially in areas with limited public transportation.
  • Ability to meet essential physical demands of position including having the physical capacity to implement supports which includes using hands to handle, finger or feel objects, tools or controls; walking, sitting, standing, bending, twisting, stooping, kneeling, crouching, pushing, pulling and reaching with hands and arms; ability to lift, carry and transport items needed for therapeutic interventions performed in a variety of environmental settings, weighing up to 25 pounds to/from sessions, as needed and ability to implement crisis intervention plan if/as needed, which may include running.

Pay Rate: $31.25/hour


Preferred Qualification Requirements (desired requirements beyond MQRs above)

  • Familiarity with START program and services
  • Experience working with families and/or social service providers
  • Verbal and/or written fluency in Spanish highly preferred; fluency in other language(s) may be preferred based on assigned region(s) and caseload

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or status as a Vietnam or disabled veteran. YAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

To ensure fairness, safeguard transparency, and promote an equitable workforce environment, YAI Network prohibits the practice of nepotism in the workforce and hiring process.

This is a full-time key personnel role subject to HFS approval. The successful candidate must bring at least ten years of experience with Medicaid information systems, data processing, and data reporting and must be able to work effectively across program operations, care management, product development, compliance, quality, security, and State stakeholders.

Responsibilities:

  • Provide overall leadership for the TCMP technology and data-management environment during implementation, readiness review, launch, and ongoing operations
  • Oversee and maintain the program's data-management system to support complete, valid, and timely collection and processing of program and Class Member information
  • Ensure the technology platform supports care-manager assignments, assessments, service plans, contacts, referrals, tasks, incidents, transition activities, service delivery, and outcomes

  • Ensure the reporting platform produces complete and accurate reports, data files, dashboards, and extracts at both aggregate and Class Member levels in formats and frequencies specified by HFS
  • Implement data-quality, validation, reconciliation, exception-management, and corrective-reporting processes to identify and resolve incomplete or inaccurate data promptly
  • Support reporting for Williams and Colbert Consent Decree compliance, care-management operations, transitions, customer service, quality assurance, subcontractor performance, and other HFS requirements
  • Lead or contribute to the System Readiness Plan, Data Security Plan, technology policies, operating procedures, and evidence required for HFS readiness review and approval
  • Demonstrate that the care-management system, reporting platform, customer-service technology, portal, and external data connections are fully functional before operational launch
  • Coordinate with the client’s product development, project management, operations, compliance, quality, security, and reporting teams to align technology delivery with program requirements
  • Provide functional oversight to the Chief Security Officer and help ensure compliance with applicable State and federal security, privacy, HIPAA, incident-response, and SOC 1 and SOC 2 requirements
  • Support analytic tools and dashboards used to monitor caseloads, acuity, productivity, program performance, service levels, and compliance in real time
  • Respond to evolving HFS reporting needs and communicate technology risks, dependencies, milestones, and corrective actions clearly to the client, S2Tech, HFS, and other stakeholders

    Required Qualifications:

    • At least ten years of experience with Medicaid information systems, data processing, and data reporting
    • Demonstrated leadership experience implementing, integrating, operating, or maintaining enterprise Medicaid or healthcare data-management platforms
    • Experience producing and submitting accurate member-level and aggregate reports for a state Medicaid agency or comparable government healthcare program
    • Strong experience with healthcare data architecture, system integration, data exchange, data quality, reconciliation, reporting, analytics, and dashboards
    • Experience leading system implementation, readiness, testing, data validation, production launch, and ongoing operational support
    • Working knowledge of HIPAA and healthcare privacy and security requirements, including experience operating within a controlled or audited environment
    • Experience working directly with state agency stakeholders, program leadership, product and engineering teams, vendors, and subcontractors
    • Ability to translate contractual requirements into system capabilities, data specifications, operational processes, and measurable deliverables
    • Strong executive communication, problem-solving, risk-management, and cross-functional leadership skills
    • Ability to work in the Chicago area and from the client's local office at least part of the time
    • Ability to satisfy HFS review and approval requirements for key personnel

    Preferred Experience:

    • Experience supporting the Illinois Medicaid program or working with the Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services
    • Experience with Medicaid care management, behavioral health, long-term services and supports, home and community-based services, or complex populations transitioning from institutional to community settings
    • Experience supporting consent-decree, court-monitor, CMS, state oversight, or regulatory reporting
    • Experience with cloud-based care-management platforms, data warehouses or lakehouses, reporting and business-intelligence tools, portals, APIs, and integration technologies
    • Experience overseeing technical, data, reporting, product-development, or information-security teams and preparing solutions for formal readiness reviews or audits

title: Director, Data Enablement & Standards
description:
Job Description Summary:

Data is increasingly central to how the North America Operating Unit (NAOU) and its bottling partners understand the market, serve customers, improve execution, and make commercial decisions. Realizing that value often requires more than technology, it requires a leader who can connect business priorities, data capabilities, operating processes, and decision-makers across a complex system.

The Director, Data Enablement & Standards will lead high-priority efforts that make data easier to understand, access, connect, and use across NAOU and the North America system. This leader will work across business teams, Bottlers, Data & AI, and enabling functions to identify barriers, shape practical solutions, establish clear ways of working, and move cross-functional priorities from ambiguity to sustained action.

Initial areas of focus are expected to include strengthening how NAOU manages and realizes value from third-party data and advancing shared data standards across the North America system. Over time, the role may take on additional data enablement priorities where stronger coordination, common approaches, and focused leadership can help the system move faster and make better decisions.


Role purpose

Lead strategic data enablement priorities that require coordination across business, technical, and system partners, translating business needs into shared standards, repeatable processes, and clear accountability. The role owns the approach, coordination, and progress on agreed priorities, while business, specialist, and technical teams retain ownership of their data, decisions, and platforms.

Key responsibilities

  • Shape the data enablement portfolio. Identify and prioritize opportunities where common approaches, stronger coordination, or focused leadership can unlock business value from data. Establish clear outcomes, roadmaps, decision rights, and measures of progress.
  • Turn complex needs into practical action. Translate business challenges into achievable data, process, standards, governance, and operating-model improvements. Develop options, clarify tradeoffs, recommend a path, and move stakeholders toward decisions.
  • Build alignment across the North America system. Bring together NAOU, Bottlers, CONA, CCBSS, and enabling functions around shared priorities. Build commitment through business value and practical recommendations.
  • Improve how data moves from need to use. Examine the processes through which data is identified, acquired, defined, maintained, accessed, shared, and applied. Resolve unclear handoffs, fragmented ownership, duplication, and other barriers that slow progress.
  • Advance shared data standards. Lead priority efforts to align definitions, hierarchies, attributes, mappings, and related ways of working where greater consistency creates meaningful business or technical value.
  • Increase the value of external data. Lead and operate how NAOU identifies, acquires, governs, shares, and uses third-party data. Connect business needs, vendor capabilities, contractual rights, costs, access, consumption, and renewal decisions while maintaining appropriate business ownership.
  • Enable responsible data access and use. Partner with Legal, Procurement, Privacy, Finance, and technical teams to translate new business, analytical, sharing, and AI use cases into clear requirements and workable decisions.
  • Build capabilities that last. Establish practical mechanisms for intake, prioritization, discovery, decision-making, adoption, and follow-through. Use Data & AI tools where they can reduce friction and improve decision support while maintaining human accountability.

Education, Experience, Skills, and Behaviors

  • Education. Bachelor's degree in Business, Data & Analytics, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience, required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
  • Relevant experience. 7+ years of relevant experience in data, analytics, data management, or related business roles, including leading cross-functional initiatives, required.
  • Data and analytics fluency. Understands datasets, definitions, hierarchies, lineage, quality, and business use. Can connect commercial needs with technical considerations and engage credibly with business and data teams.
  • Influence without authority. Builds trust across organizations with different incentives. Makes the case for change, negotiates practical commitments, and secures buy-in rather than relying on escalation or formal authority.
  • Decision-oriented leadership. Frames problems, develops options, recommends a path, and helps stakeholders make decisions. Turns agreement into named owners, clear expectations, and follow-through.
  • Independent ownership and judgment. Determines what needs to happen next, establishes priorities, anticipates issues, and drives outcomes without detailed direction. Knows when to act, seek input, or escalate.
  • Process design and continuous improvement. Can map a process across teams, diagnose root causes, and translate findings into improvements that people can adopt and sustain.
  • Vendor and commercial understanding. Experience with vendor relationships, data agreements, or related commercial processes. Can identify requirements and restrictions and work effectively with Legal and Procurement specialists.
  • Practical capability building. Comfortable creating structure where it does not yet exist. Starts with a workable approach, tests it, and improves it without overbuilding.

title: Supervisor, FlexForce Programs
description:
Location: Orlando, FL | Full Time | Pay Range: $55,996.43 - $65,878.15/YR (Based on experience and qualifications)

Develop Talent. Build Readiness. Power Live Events.

Every great event depends on skilled technicians who are ready to perform when it matters most. As Supervisor, FlexForce Programs, you'll help build that foundation by developing emerging technical talent, creating pathways for growth, and ensuring technicians are prepared to support exceptional live event experiences.

This is an opportunity to shape the future of our workforce while making a lasting impact on the people behind the production. If you're passionate about coaching others, building scalable training programs, and helping technicians grow their careers, you'll find meaningful work here.

Why This Role Matters

Our FlexForce program is more than a staffing initiative. It's a talent development pipeline that helps aspiring technicians build careers in live events. In this role, you'll guide technicians through every stage of their journey, from recruiting and onboarding to skills development, scheduling, progression tracking, and career advancement.

Your work will directly influence technician readiness, workforce planning, and the long-term success of the teams supporting events across Orlando, Las Vegas, and Nashville.

About LMG

LMG is a full-service event technology provider delivering video, audio, lighting, and LED solutions for corporate events, conventions, and live productions. Founded in 1984, LMG has grown from a one-room video rental office into a trusted partner for Fortune 500 companies across the nation and worldwide. As part of the ETP family of brands, we go Beyond Technology by providing innovative solutions you can trust.

What You'll Do

Develop and Coach Future Technical Talent

  • Lead the growth and development of FlexForce Technicians through individualized coaching and mentorship.
  • Conduct regular one-on-one meetings to discuss technician progress, career goals, challenges, and development opportunities.
  • Provide timely feedback, coaching, and performance guidance that supports professional growth.
  • Administer progressive discipline when necessary while maintaining a constructive, development-focused approach.
  • Partner with technical leadership to establish clear advancement pathways aligned with organizational needs and technician goals.

Build and Manage Technician Training Programs

  • Design, facilitate, and continuously improve training programs focused on technical execution, troubleshooting, signal flow, breakout room operations, and client interaction.
  • Coordinate hands-on learning experiences, shadowing opportunities, and cross-functional exposure for technicians.
  • Research and implement new training opportunities that strengthen workforce capabilities.
  • Update phase progression requirements, discipline checklists, and development materials as business needs evolve.
  • Stay current on industry trends, technical standards, and emerging technologies to enhance workforce readiness.

Oversee Technician Readiness and Progression

  • Monitor technician progress through established phases and disciplines, including required hours, competencies, certifications, and developmental checklists.
  • Ensure all technicians receive the onboarding, mentorship, and support needed to succeed.
  • Communicate progression milestones and advancement opportunities clearly and consistently.
  • Maintain technician records, certifications, proficiencies, experience levels, and developmental documentation.

Coordinate Workforce Planning and Scheduling

  • Maintain technician schedules across Orlando, Las Vegas, and Nashville markets.
  • Assign technicians based on event requirements while balancing workforce utilization and development opportunities.
  • Collaborate with operational leaders to ensure staffing levels meet current and future business needs.
  • Verify technician timecards and ensure accurate workforce records.
  • Strategically align technicians with opportunities that strengthen technical skills and broaden experience.

Support Recruiting and Program Growth

  • Conduct outreach to local schools, colleges, trade programs, and community organizations to build a strong technician talent pipeline.
  • Review applications and resumes, participate in interviews, and coordinate hiring activities for new FlexForce Technicians.
  • Promote awareness of part-time and full-time opportunities throughout the ETP family of brands.
  • Support workforce growth initiatives that strengthen technician recruitment, retention, and long-term career development.

Partner Across the Organization

  • Work closely with Operations leadership to ensure technicians receive consistent support and developmental guidance.
  • Collaborate with Show Services, Technical Services, and Operations teams to support workforce readiness and event success.
  • Educate new operational leaders on program objectives, technician progression processes, and workforce development expectations.
  • Coordinate travel arrangements for technicians supporting events nationwide.

What You Bring

  • Experience leading technical teams within live events, AV production, hospitality technology, or similar technical environments.
  • Proven success in coaching, mentoring, workforce development, training, or technician leadership.
  • Experience coordinating schedules, staffing assignments, or workforce deployment.
  • Strong understanding of live event technology, breakout room operations, troubleshooting, signal flow, and technical execution.
  • Experience developing, facilitating, or managing structured training programs.
  • Strong organizational, communication, leadership, and relationship-building skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt in an event-driven environment.
  • Service-oriented mindset with strong problem-solving capabilities.
  • Passion for helping people grow and succeed in their careers.

Why You'll Love It Here

  • Help shape the next generation of live event professionals.
  • Build innovative training and workforce development programs that create lasting impact.
  • Partner with experienced technical leaders across multiple markets.
  • Join a culture that values mentorship, growth, collaboration, and operational excellence.
  • Support exciting productions and events while helping technicians develop meaningful careers.
  • Expand your own leadership, coaching, and workforce development expertise.

Benefits

Medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, flexible spending account, 401(k) with company contribution, paid time off, and company holidays.

Ready to Go Beyond Technology?

If you're passionate about developing talent, building workforce readiness, and creating opportunities for future technical professionals, we'd like to hear from you. Apply today and help power the people behind unforgettable live events.
